everything, all of it (neuter of весь); still, all the time (as adverb)
yes; right?, isn't it? (tag question); come on (emphatic)
for, intended for (+ genitive); for the sake of, for the purpose of
for, in exchange for (+ accusative); behind, beyond (+ instrumental)
I know (знать, impf. — to know; no true pf. partner; cf. узнать, to find out)
and; both ... and ... (repeated); also, even (for emphasis)
how; like, as (in the same way as); as soon as, when
me (я in the genitive/accusative; у меня — I have)
to me, for me; me (я in the dative/prepositional — мне холодно, I'm cold)
on, at (+ prepositional); onto, to (+ accusative, motion); for (a period)
no; there is no, there isn't; not have (with genitive)
but, yet
about, of (with the prepositional); oh! (exclamation)
he; it (standing in for any masculine noun)
with (+ instrumental); from, off, since (+ genitive)
so, like this, in that way; so, so much (to such a degree); so, then
you (ты in the genitive/accusative; у тебя — you have)
that, that one (neuter of тот); then (если…, то…); the fact that (то, что)
you (one person, informal — friends, family; polite or plural is вы)
this, that; this is, that is; it
he was, she was (past of kuwa 'to be')
so, then, well (opening a sentence); bus (5/6, pl. mabasi); enough!, stop!
so, thus, in that way; therefore (kwa hivyo); those (class 8 things just mentioned)
that person, that one (class 1 — the one just mentioned or near you)
up, above, on top; on top of, over (juu ya); about, concerning
like, as (comparison); if, whether; about, roughly (with a number)
with, by, by means of (kwa basi = by bus); for, because of (asante kwa msaada = thanks for the help)
but, however, yet (joining a contrast to what was just said)
matters, affairs, things going on (class 5/6, sg. jambo); Mambo? = How's it going?
one, a single (class 1/3/11: mtu mmoja = one person); a certain one, someone
and; with (kuwa na, to have); by (the doer after a passive verb)
with him, with her; and he, and she (na + yeye, for a class 1 person)
his, her, its (with class 1, 2, 3 and 11 nouns: mtoto wake = his child); also wives (class 1/2, sg. mke)
those, those over there (class 2, away from both speaker and hearer)
people, persons; human beings (class 1/2, sg. mtu)
all, all of (with class 2: watu wote = all the people)
of, belonging to (with class 4, 6, 9 nouns: nyumba ya mwalimu = the teacher's house)
his, her, its (with class 4, 6 and 9 nouns: nyumba yake = his/her house)
your, yours (of you all; with class 4, 6 and 9 nouns: nyumba yenu = your house)
that, that one over there (with class 1 nouns — a person or animal at a distance: yule mtu = that person)
of, belonging to (with class 10 plural nouns: nyumba za watu = people's houses)
I, me (informal; used mostly by women)
this, this one (standing alone); here
hello, hi; goodbye — the all-purpose greeting, with ครับ or ค่ะ added
or; (sentence-final yes-no question particle: …is it? / really? — spoken เหรอ, รึ)
in a moment, shortly; wait, hold on; or else, otherwise (warning)
but, however; only, just; since, from (a time)
and (formal/written; between nouns, speech often uses กับ instead)
already, done (sentence-final, marks completion); then, and then
yes, that's right; to be so, to be the case (negated with ไม่)
not (before a verb or adjective); no
and (between words, phrases or clauses); contracts to 't after a vowel-final word (dalawampu't isa)
why?; how come? (answered with kasi or dahil; kung bakit = the reason why)
if (hypothetical; kapag = whenever); whether; kung sino/ano "whoever/whatever"
or; or else (o kaya); spoken sentence-opener "so"/"here" to get attention
yes (casual); opo is the polite form to elders; oo nga "yes, exactly"
how?, in what way; paano kung "what if" (how much is magkano, not paano)
but; however (conversational; ngunit and subalit are the formal equivalents)
who? (the ang-set question word; nino = by whom, kanino = whose, to whom)
me (ben as the object of a verb: beni bekle, wait for me)
my; mine; it's me, I am the one (as a predicate)
a, an (before a noun); one (the number)
this; this one; it (bu as the object of a verb)
too, also; and, and then; say! (command from demek)
yes; yes, that's right (agreeing or confirming); right then, so (opening a turn)
come on!, let's go!
come on!, let's go!
no; no, thank you (declining); as a noun (hayr-): good, benefit, charity
good; well (with a verb); fine, in good health
what; how, what a…! (in exclamations); ne…ne… neither…nor
why; what for; reason, cause (as a noun)
that (someone or something) is, or was (introduces a 'that…' clause after know, say, think)
him; her; it; that one (o as the object of a verb)
to you; for you (singular, informal; also 'you' after verbs that take the dative)
you (singular, informal, as the object of a verb: seni seviyorum, I love you)
your; yours (singular, informal)
OK, all right, agreed; complete, whole; done, finished
there is, there are; have, has (with a possessor); present, available
and (joining words, phrases or whole clauses)
there is no, there aren't; doesn't have; no (as an answer)
people, persons; human beings (class 1/2, sg. umntu)
men, grown males; husbands (class 9/6, sg. indoda)
eyes (class 5/6, sg. iliso)
behind, at the back; after (in emva kwa- 'after, behind'; emva koko 'after that')
that, those (before any noun, which drops its first vowel: loo mntu 'that person')
law; rule, regulation; commandment (class 3/4, pl. imithetho)
son; the Son of God in Christian texts (class 1a/2a, pl. oonyana)
God; a god, deity (class 1a/2a, pl. oothixo)
we (subject pronoun); will (á before a verb); him, her, it (á, echoing a verb that ends in a)
plural marker àwọn, placed before a noun; they, them (emphatic pronoun)
if, when (bí); like, as, how (bí); to give birth to (bí)
to use; with, by means of — sets up the instrument before a second verb
it, him, her — object pronoun after a verb ending in i; the í of kì í "does not usually, never"
a, a certain; one (after the noun: ọjọ́ kan "one day"); kàn to touch, to concern
that, should (kí, subjunctive); what? (kí ni); to greet (kí)
not (kò, before the verb); to gather, to pack up (kó)
to (láti, infinitive marker before a verb); from (a place); since (a time)
is/are doing — ń before a verb marks ongoing action; also "I" (n̄, variant of mo)
is, it is (ni, copula and focus); at, in, on (ní); to have (ní)
he, she, it (ó); you (o, subject); not (ò, short for kò); final o for emphasis
to see; to find, to get; to look like, to appear
to, toward (sí, with motion); and then (sì, links clauses); there is (in kò sí)
or — joins two alternatives (written tàbí in full)
already, have done (ti, before a verb); who, which, that (tí); of, belonging to
they (wọ́n, subject); them (wọn, after a verb); their (wọn, after a noun)
this (placed after the noun, written yìí in full); yí to turn, to change
you (plural or polite, as subject); you (singular, as object after the verb)
you (one person), as the object of a verb; him, her, it after a verb ending in ọ
not — a very common shortened form of δεν before a consonant (Δε θέλω — I don't want to); in formal Greek also μεν … δε — on the other hand
only, just; with a weak pronoun: alone, by oneself (μόνο του — by himself)
always; τα πάντα — everything, all things (ξέρω τα πάντα — I know everything)
children — plural of το παιδί (τα παιδιά μας — our children); also as an address to a group: guys, folks
other, another; else (τίποτα άλλο — nothing else); more (κι άλλο χρόνο — more time); after a negative: any more
you go — 2nd person singular of πάω (Πού πας; — where are you going?); an identical archaic πας — every, all — survives only in frozen formal phrases
it is needed, one needs to (δε χρειάζεται να — there is no need to); also, as the 3rd singular of χρειάζομαι, he, she or it needs (το ρολόι μου χρειάζεται επισκευή — my watch needs repair)
seen — the nonfinite form of βλέπω, after έχω (δεν τον έχω δει — I have not seen him) and after να or θα (να δει — for him to see)
said, told — the nonfinite form of λέω, after έχω (δεν έχουμε πει ναι — we have not said yes) and after να or θα (να πει — for him to say)
some, any (du pain = some bread); of the, from the (de + le: la fin du film)
past participle of faire — done, made (c'est bien fait); also third-person singular present: il fait = he does, he makes, it is (weather); (as noun, m.) a fact, en fait = in fact
third-person singular present of aller — goes (ça va = it's fine, how are you?); il va + infinitive = he is going to (on va voir = we'll see); also the singular imperative: va = go!
second-person singular present of avoir — you have (tu as); also the helper for the past: tu as mangé = you ate; (as noun, m.) an ace, a card of value 1
third-person singular present and past participle of dire — says, said (dit-il = he said; j'ai tout dit = I've said everything); (as adj.) known as, alias
better (comparative of bien); le mieux = the best; faire de son mieux = to do one's best; il vaut mieux = it is better to
third-person singular present subjunctive of être — (that it) be: il faut que ce soit fait = it has to be done; quoi que ce soit = anything at all; soit A soit B = either A or B
less, fewer (comparative of peu); le moins = the least; au moins = at least; à moins que = unless; also minus (in sums and clock times)
stays, remains — from rester (je reste, il reste; reste ici = stay here); il reste beaucoup à faire = much remains to be done; (as noun, m.) the rest, the remainder
passes, pass — from passer (je passe, il passe; passe-moi le sel = pass me the salt); que se passe-t-il = what is going on; (as noun, f.) a pass, mot de passe = password
past participle of prendre — took, taken (j'ai pris = I took); (as adj.) taken, occupied (la place est prise)
(f.) share, portion, slice; de ma part = from me, on my behalf; quelque part = somewhere; à part = apart from; also il/elle part = he/she leaves (from partir)
(f.) part, portion (en partie = partly, faire partie de = to be part of); a game, a match (une partie de cartes); also elle est partie = she has left (feminine past participle of partir)
asks, ask — from demander (il demande, demande-lui = ask him); se demander = to wonder (je me demande = I wonder); (as noun, f.) a request, demand
leave, let — from laisser (il laisse; laisse-moi = let me, leave me alone); laisse tomber = forget it; (as noun, f.) a leash
past participle of partir — gone, left (il est parti = he left); (as noun, m.) a political party; parti pris = a bias
third-person singular future of avoir — will have (il aura = he will have; il y aura = there will be); (as noun, f.) an aura

do — the stem of करना, standing before रहा, सकना and the vector verbs (कर रहे हैं — are doing, कर सकते हो — you can do); also the conjunctive participle -कर, having done; and, as a literary noun, hand, arm (m.); tax (m.)

gave — masculine singular perfective of देना (मैंने कुछ नहीं दिया — I gave nothing); as a completive vector after a stem it says the act was carried through: कर दिया — went and did it, छोड़ दिया — dropped it; also an oil lamp (m.), also spelled दीया
said — masculine singular perfective of कहना (उसने कहा — he said; तुमने क्या कहा? — what did you say?); also a noun (m.): someone's word or bidding, as in कहा मानना — to do as one is told
two (2); also give! — the तुम imperative of देना, and the same form as a completive vector: दे दो — hand it over, छोड़ दो — let it go, कर दो — just do it
give — the stem of देना, standing before सकना, रहा and the vector verbs (नहीं दे सकता — I can't give, दे दो — give it here); also second/third-person singular present subjunctive: may give
is, happens, tends to be — masculine singular habitual participle of होना (ऐसा होता है — that is how it is; कुछ नहीं होता — nothing happens); also the counterfactual, होता तो — had it been so

gave — feminine singular perfective of देना, agreeing with a feminine object under ने (उसने चेतावनी दी — he gave a warning); most often the completive vector taking that same agreement: नौकरी छोड़ दी — quit the job; also short for दीदी, elder sister (f.)
whole, complete, full — feminine of पूरा, agreeing with a feminine noun (पूरी रात — all night, पूरी तरह से — completely); also a puri (f.), the small deep-fried bread
contraction of a + il; to the, at the — al lavoro 'at work', andare al mare 'to go to the sea'; also with (an ingredient): pasta al pomodoro
you (after prepositions: con te, per te; and in comparisons: come te); replaces ti before lo, la, li, le, ne: te lo dico 'I'm telling you'
third-person singular imperfect indicative of essere; he/she/it was: era solo 'he was alone', non c'era 'he wasn't there'; also a noun: era, age, epoch
done, made (past participle of fare): l'ho fatto 'I did it'; also a noun: fact, event — il fatto è che 'the fact is that'
of it, of them, about it (partitive): ne ho una 'I have one of them', non ne so nulla 'I know nothing about it'; from there, away: me ne vado 'I'm off'
contraction of a + la; to the, at the — alla stazione 'to the station', alla fine 'in the end'; also in the style of, à la: pollo alla cacciatora
been (past participle of essere): sono stato a Roma 'I have been to Rome'; stayed (past participle of stare); also a noun: state, country, condition
more, most (comparative of molto): più grande 'bigger', il più veloce 'the fastest'; with non, no longer, anymore: non è più solo 'he isn't alone anymore'; plus (in arithmetic)
sir, gentleman; Mr (as a title): grazie, signore 'thank you, sir'; ladies (plural of signora): prima le signore 'ladies first'; the Lord, God (il Signore); lord, master (a ruler)
others, other people; other (masculine plural of altro): gli altri ragazzi 'the other boys', dove sono gli altri? 'where are the others?'; as a literary singular pronoun, someone else
taken, got, caught (past participle of prendere): dove l'hai preso? 'where did you get it?'; taken, occupied (of a seat); busy, preoccupied (of a person)

face (of a person or an animal): lavati la faccia 'wash your face', faccia a faccia 'face to face'; also from fare — the singular present subjunctive (voglio che tu faccia 'I want you to do') and the formal Lei imperative: faccia pure 'go right ahead'
heard; felt (past participle of sentire): non ho sentito 'I didn't hear'; as an adjective, heartfelt, sincere: un sentito grazie
beautiful, lovely (feminine singular of bello): la vita è bella 'life is beautiful'; also a noun: a beauty, a belle; the decider (deciding match)
end (la fine): alla fine 'in the end', la fine del film; in the compound il fine settimana, weekend; purpose, aim (il fine): il fine giustifica i mezzi; as an adjective, thin, fine, refined
thought (past participle of pensare): ci ho pensato molto 'I thought about it a lot'; as an adjective, well thought-out: ben pensato
gone, went (feminine singular past participle of andare): è andata a casa 'she went home', se n'è andata 'she left'; also a noun: the outward journey — andata e ritorno 'round trip'
spoken, talked (past participle of parlare): hai parlato con lei? 'did you speak with her?'; as a noun, the spoken language; as an adjective, with sound (of a film)
come (past participle of venire): è venuto ieri 'he came yesterday', non è venuto nessuno 'nobody came'; as a noun, a newcomer: il nuovo venuto
first/second/third-person singular present subjunctive of stare: spero che tu stia bene 'I hope you are well'; also the formal Lei imperative: stia calmo 'stay calm'; a rare noun, hutch, coop
a little, a bit (short for 조금); also the softener in a request or command, roughly just or please
the fact that, the one that — 것이 contracted (거 plus the subject marker 이), after a -는/-은/-을 form: 가는 게 좋아요; a crab
do, does, do it — 하다 in the intimate style (다시 해, do it again), and the base of 해요/했어요; the sun, sunlight
the fact that, the one that, as object — 것을 contracted (거 plus the object marker 를); also the guess ending -(으)ㄹ걸, I bet, probably; 3 points in the game of yut
come, come here — 오다 in the intimate style; and, with (the particle after a vowel: 커피와 빵); wow (exclamation)
if one does, when one does — 하다 with the conditional -(으)면 (어떻게 하면, how can I…); rarely, the underside, bottom surface
seen, that one saw — 보다 in the past determiner form; also the -아/어 본 적 있다 pattern, to have ever done something; as a prefix (本), main, original
new, fresh (before a noun: 새 차, a new car); a bird
will see, to see — 보다 in the -(으)ㄹ determiner form (볼 수 있어요, can see); a cheek; a ball
will know, to know — 알다 in the -(으)ㄹ determiner form (알 것 같아요, I think I know; 알 바 아니다, none of my business); an egg, fish roe; a counter for small round things (계란 두 알)
will lift, hold, enter, or cost — 들다 in the -(으)ㄹ determiner form (돈이 들 거야, it will cost money; 예를 들 수 있어요, can give an example); also the plural marker -들 (사람들); a field, a plain
been (past participle of a fi: a fost “it was”, am fost “I have been”); former, ex- (fostul primar)
he/she/it can, is able to (a putea: nu poate veni “he can't come”); maybe, perhaps (as an adverb: poate da, poate nu)
I can; they can (a putea: nu pot “I can't”, pot să vin “I can come”); rarely a noun: the pot, the stakes in a card game (neuter)
seen (past participle of a vedea: am văzut “I saw”, nu l-am văzut “I didn't see him”); as a noun: sight, seeing (neuter)
takes; take! (3rd person singular and imperative of a lua: ia loc “have a seat”, ia-mă cu tine “take me with you”); as an interjection: hey, look here
taken (past participle of a lua: l-am luat “I took it”, a luat-o “she took it / she went”); as a noun: taking (neuter)
(that) I be — first-person singular subjunctive of a fi (vreau să fiu “I want to be”, să fiu sincer “to be honest”); son (m.)
found (past participle of a găsi: am găsit “I found”, cum m-ai găsit? “how did you find me?”); as a noun: finding (neuter)
the ones, those (masculine plural of cel); forms the superlative: cei mai buni “the best”
the day (definite form of zi, f.: bună ziua “good day”, ziua ta “your birthday”); as an adverb: during the day, by day
I come; they come (a veni: vin acum “I'm coming”, ei vin “they're coming”); wine (neuter)
begun, started (past participle of a începe: a început să plouă “it started to rain”); a beginning, a start (neuter noun)
taken, carried; gone (past participle of a duce: s-a dus acasă “he went home”); as an adjective: departed, absent-minded
the time, the occasion (definite form of dată, f.: data viitoare “next time”, de data asta “this time”); the date, the calendar date; also a verb: a data “to date from”
worries, cares (plural of grijă, f.); a-și face griji “to worry”: nu-ți face griji “don't worry”
the night (definite form of noapte, f.: noaptea trecută “last night”, în noaptea aceea “that night”); as an adverb: at night, by night
left, let (past participle of a lăsa: m-a lăsat să plec “he let me go”, lăsat singur “left alone”); abandoned, dropped
new (feminine singular of nou: o casă nouă “a new house”, o nouă zi “a new day”); nine; (to) us (stressed dative of noi: nouă ne place “we like it”)
him, of him (он in the genitive/accusative; его нет — he's not here); his, its (one invariable possessive form for every gender)
there is, there are; у меня есть — I have (the one surviving present form of быть, dropped elsewhere); to eat (impf.; pf. съесть)
than; instead of, rather (лучше, чем ничего — better than nothing); what, with what — что in the instrumental (Чем ты занимаешься? — What do you do?; Чем могу помочь? — How can I help?)
that, it — тот/то in the prepositional (о том, что… — about the fact that…; дело в том, что… — the thing is…; в том доме — in that house); a volume, tome (m.) of a book
there it is, here you go, that is just it; you see, well (discourse marker); also the locative of iş: at work, in a job or matter
even, so much as; (after a verb) already; archaic variant of ile: with, together with
second-person singular imperative of etmek: do it!, make it! (in light verbs: yardım et — help!, dikkat et — be careful!); also meat, flesh
quotative converb of demek: saying, that (marks reported speech and thought); called, named (X diye bir şey: a thing called X); so that, in order to
still, yet (the circumflex of hâlâ is routinely dropped in writing); paternal aunt, father's sister
second-person singular imperative of almak: take!, get!, buy! (onu al — pick it up); also (poetic) blood red, scarlet, as in al bayrak, the Turkish flag
first-person singular possessive of hayat: my life; as a term of address: darling, sweetheart
second-person singular negative imperative of etmek: do not do, do not (merak etme — do not worry, rahatsız etme — do not disturb); also the verbal noun of etmek: doing, making

did (third-person singular present indicative of anar; with an infinitive it makes the everyday past: va dir, he said); he/she/it goes: com va?, how is it going?; also vain, in the fixed phrase en va, in vain
I/he/she/it was (first/third-person singular imperfect indicative of ser); also (f.) era, age
I am (first-person singular present indicative of estar — state, location, ongoing action); also (m.) hockey stick
done, made (past participle of fer); also (m.) fact, deed: de fet, in fact
he/she/it does, makes (third-person singular present indicative of fer); ago: fa dos anys, two years ago; also (m.) fa, the fourth note of the scale
you go (second-person singular present indicative of anar; with an infinitive it makes the everyday past: vas dir, you said); also (m.) glass, tumbler
been (past participle of estar and of ser); also (m.) state, condition; the State, government
he/she/it can, is able to (third-person singular present indicative of poder); also (m.) pot, jar, tin
you have (second-person singular present indicative of tenir); also tense, taut
said, told (past participle of dir); also (m.) finger, toe
he/she/it knows, you (vostè) know (third-person singular present indicative of saber); also (m.) common heather
it happens; he/she/it passes (third-person singular present indicative of passar); pass!, come in! (second-person singular imperative); also (f.) stride; outbreak of illness
woman (f.); wife; also gives (third-person singular present indicative of donar, written dóna before the 2016 reform)
dead; died (past participle of morir, also used as an adjective); also (f.) death: la pena de mort, the death penalty
happened, passed (past participle of passar); last, past: el mes passat, last month; also (m.) the past
door (f.); gate, gateway; also he/she/it carries, brings, wears (third-person singular present indicative of portar)
we are (first-person plural present indicative of ser); also shallow (of water)
which?, what? (feminine singular of quin); also (f.) quina, a bingo-like game played at Christmas
heard, felt (past participle of sentir); also (m.) sense; meaning: no té sentit, it makes no sense
found (past participle of trobar); also (m.) tawny pipit (the bird)
I say, I tell (first-person singular present indicative of dir): em dic Anna, my name is Anna; also (m.) dyke, sea wall
finished, ended (past participle of acabar); also (m.) finish, surface coating
I do, I make (first-person singular present indicative of fer); also (m.) beech (the tree)
voice (f.): en veu alta, aloud; also he/she/it sees (third-person singular present indicative of veure): es veu que, apparently
alive, living; lively, vivid; also he/she/it lives (third-person singular present indicative of viure)
you are (second-person plural present indicative of ser); also (m.) pay, salary
hands (f., plural of mà); also tame, docile
we do, we make (first-person plural present indicative of fer); also (m.) dung, manure
left, let (past participle of deixar); also slovenly, unkempt
he/she/it speaks, talks (third-person singular present indicative of parlar); speak! (second-person singular imperative); also (f.) speech, a community's way of speaking

do!, make! (second-person singular imperative of fer); (that I/he) did, would do (first/third-person singular imperfect subjunctive of fer): em va dir que fes això, he told me to do this; also cleft, split; (m.) fez
speaking (gerund of parlar): estic parlant, I am talking; also (m., f.) speaker, one who speaks
he/she/it thinks (third-person singular present indicative of pensar); think! (second-person singular imperative); also (f.) mind, the faculty of thought
for (indicating recipient, purpose or benefit); in exchange for, in return for
her, their, your (polite Ihr) — possessive: ihr Vater, her/their father; (to) her — dative of sie; you (plural, familiar) — subject pronoun

said, told - past participle of decir (que has dicho? - what did you say?); mentioned, aforementioned; also el dicho, a saying or proverb

gone - past participle of ir (se ha ido, he has gone); also ido: out of it, absent-minded

list, roll; ready, clever - feminine of listo (ya estoy lista, I'm ready); stripe
know: I know; you know in weet je; he/she/it knows (present of weten); as a noun, awareness (geen weet hebben van)
can, to be able to: I can; he/she/it can; you can in kan je (present of kunnen); also a noun, jug, pot
want: I want; he/she/it wants; you want in wil je (present of willen); also a noun, will, willpower
where, in which place (waar is hij?); true (dat is niet waar — that's not true); where, the place that
come: I come; come! (present and imperative of komen); also a noun, bowl, basin
more (comparative of veel); niet meer — not anymore, no longer; also a noun, lake
late (not early); also let, leave: I let; let…! (present and imperative of laten — laat maar, laat zien)
once, one time; sometime; a softening particle in requests and imperatives (kijk eens, wacht eens even); nog eens — again; het eens zijn met — to agree with
to let, to allow; to have something done (ik laat het zien — I'll show it); laten we… — let's…; to leave (as it is)
sit; be (located, contained): I sit; he/she/it sits (present of zitten); as a noun, a sitting
keep, hold: I keep, I hold (present of houden); ik hou van je — I love you (houden van); hou op! — stop it!
look, watch: I look; look! (present and imperative of kijken); also a noun, view, outlook (kijk op iets)
wait: wait! (imperative of wachten); I wait, he/she/it waits; also a noun, guard duty, watch
she; they (the stressed forms, used for emphasis or contrast; ze when unstressed)
give: I give; give! (present and imperative of geven)
were: we/you/they were (plural past of zijn); as a noun, goods, wares (plural of waar)
better (comparative of goed); well again, recovered from illness (ik ben weer beter)
stands: he/she/it stands, you stand (jij staat); is located, is situated (present of staan); also a noun: state, condition (in staat zijn — to be able to), and the State
to, towards — the form tot takes in ertoe, waartoe and in separable verbs (toegeven, toedoen); aan iets toe zijn — to be ready for, due for; shut, closed (de deur is toe); toe maar! — go on!
things (plural of ding); rarely a verb, dingen naar — to vie for, compete for
good — the -e form of goed (een goede vader, het goede boek); het goede — what is good, the good
worries, cares (plural of zorg — maak je geen zorgen, don't worry); to look after, take care of (zorgen voor); to see to it, make sure (zorgen dat)
question, query; demand (for goods); also I ask / ask! from vragen — ik vraag me af, I wonder
I hear (ik hoor iets; hoor je mij? — from horen); ik hoor te … — I am supposed to, I ought to; also the softening particle: sure, all right (ja hoor, nee hoor)
I believe, I think (ik geloof van wel); believe! (from geloven — geloof me); as a noun: belief, faith, religion
sat, was sitting (past singular of zitten — ze zat naast me, she sat next to me; ik zat vast, I was stuck); fed up with, sick of (iets zat zijn); drunk (informal)
asked (past singular of vragen — ik vroeg hem naar zijn naam); early (te vroeg; vroeg of laat, sooner or later)
stop!, quit! (imperative of stoppen, usually stop met … — stop met praten); I stop; as a noun: a plug, a stopper; a fuse
I get, I receive (ik krijg wat ik wil); get! (imperative of krijgen); (archaic) war
days (plural of dag — drie dagen geleden); to show up, turn up (op komen dagen); to summon to court
made, done (past participle of maken — ik heb het zelf gemaakt; van hout gemaakt, made of wood); as an adjective: artificial, affected
I look for, I am searching (ik zoek mijn vrienden); look for!, seek! (from zoeken — zoek dekking, take cover); op zoek naar — in search of, looking for; as an adjective: lost, missing
I call, I phone (ik bel je later terug); call! (imperative of bellen — bel de politie); as a noun: bell, doorbell
best (superlative of goed — je best doen, to do one's best); quite, rather (het is best koud vandaag); dear (beste …, in an address)
out of it, out of there (er + uit — haal de stekker eruit); eruitzien: to look, to appear (hoe ziet zij eruit?); as a shout: out! get out!
pack, package; suit (set of clothes); also grab!, take! (imperative of pakken — pak je spullen, pak 'm)
I help; help me!, help out! (imperative of helpen — help me deze lading uit te laden); also the cry help!
later, afterwards (comparative of laat — ik bel je later terug; drie uur later); when I'm grown up (als ik later groot ben); as an adjective: later, subsequent
talk, speak — the present tense of praten (je praat te veel; praat niet zo tegen hem); as a noun: talk, chatter
to call, to phone (ik moet bellen — I have to make a call); to ring (a bell)
be! (imperative of zijn — wees niet bang, don't be afraid; wees voorzichtig, be careful); pointed, turned down (past of wijzen); as a noun: an orphan
make sure!, see to it! (zorg dat …, zorg ervoor dat …); take care of! (zorg voor …, from zorgen); as a noun: care, concern; healthcare
things, matters, affairs (plural of zaak — dat soort zaken, stand van zaken); business (zaken doen; bemoei je met je eigen zaken); Affairs, in ministry names (Buitenlandse Zaken)
to; for; in order to (destination, recipient, purpose: vou para casa, para você, para fazer); also stop!, stops (from parar)
I am (temporary states, feelings and locations — from estar); (European, answering the telephone) hello
let's (vamos ver = let's see, vamos lá = let's go); we're going to (forms the future: vamos fazer); we go, we are going (from ir)
to the, at the (a + a, feminine singular — the crase à: à noite, à casa dela); in set phrases, in the manner of (à moda de)
was, used to be (I, he, she, it, você — imperfect of ser); (as a noun, f.) era, age
they are; you are (plural — from ser); it's (telling the time: são 9h15); also Saint (before a man's name), and (adj.) sound, healthy
had; used to have (I, he, she, it, você — imperfect of ter); tinha que = had to; (as a noun, f.) ringworm
(to) him, (to) her, (to) you (indirect object of the verb: eu lhe disse = I told him); his, her, your (with body parts and belongings: lavei-lhe as mãos)
work; job (m.); I work (from trabalhar)
waits; hopes; expects (he, she, você — from esperar); wait! (as a command); (as a noun, f.) wait (sala de espera = waiting room)
they go, they're going; you (plural) go (from ir); they're going to (forms the future: vão chegar); (as an adjective) vain, futile (em vão = in vain)
look!, look at (olha isso = look at this); look, hey (opening a remark in speech); he, she looks (from olhar)
return (f.); back (de volta: quero meu dinheiro de volta); a walk, a spin (dar uma volta); also comes back, returns (from voltar)
thank you (said by a woman; a man says obrigado); (as a participle, f.) obliged, forced (foi obrigada a = she was made to)
walks; goes (he, she, você — from andar); come on!, get moving! (as a command)
between; among (entre nós = between us, entre as duas cidades); also come in! (from entrar)
new (feminine of novo: uma casa nova); young, younger (ela é mais nova que ele)
help, aid (f.); helps (he, she, você — from ajudar)
dead (ele está morto); killed (foi morto = he was killed — past participle of matar as well as of morrer)
bill, check (f.: a conta, por favor); account (bank or online); sum, calculation; tomar conta de = to look after; also tells, counts (from contar)
ma'am, madam (f.); a senhora = you (polite, to a woman — takes he/she verb forms); lady
speaks, talks (he, she, você — from falar: você fala inglês?); (as a noun, f.) speech
state (m.: of a country — cada estado tem seu governo); condition (em mau estado, estado civil); been (tem estado = has been — past participle of estar)
bigger, larger, taller (comparative of grande); biggest, greatest (o maior); a maior parte = most of
arrives, gets there (he, she, você — from chegar); já chega! = that's enough!
I think (from pensar: penso que = I think that); (European, as a noun, m.) a dressing, a band-aid
much, a lot of; many (feminine of muito: muita gente = a lot of people)
came (he, she, você — preterite of vir); (as a noun, m.) vein, seam (of ore)
look!, have a look (singular imperative of schauen; schau mal — take a look); Schau (die) — show, display, exhibition
on it, on that, of it (colloquial form of darauf; es kommt drauf an — it depends; ich freu mich drauf — I'm looking forward to it); (slang) drauf sein — to be high

to put, to place, to set (causative of sitzen; unter Druck setzen — to put under pressure; ein Komma setzen — to place a comma); sich setzen — to sit down; to settle, to precipitate; to bet, to wager (auf + acc.)
call!, call (singular imperative of rufen; ruf mich an — call me); Ruf (der) — reputation; call, shout, cry
I look for, I am looking for; look for! (first-person singular present and imperative of suchen; ich suche Arbeit — I'm looking for work); Suche (die) — search

good (strong/mixed nominative/accusative neuter singular of gut; ein gutes Buch — a good book; gutes Wetter — good weather); Gutes — something good, good things (nominalised: nichts Gutes im Schilde führen)
days (dative plural of Tag; vor drei Tagen — three days ago; in diesen Tagen — these days); tagen (verb) — to meet, to convene; to dawn

rather (eher … als — rather … than; eher niedlich als schön); fairly, relatively, somewhat (weakened degree); sooner, earlier (comparative of bald/früh; je eher, desto besser — the sooner the better; nicht eher … bis — not until)
try! (singular imperative of versuchen; versuch es noch einmal — give it another try); Versuch (der) — attempt, try; experiment, test, trial
I hate (first-person singular present of hassen; ich hasse Kaffee — I hate coffee); Hasse (die) — (Austrian, colloquial) Burenwurst, a grilled sausage

to lay, to put, to place (causative of liegen; legen Sie die Hände auf den Kopf — put your hands on your head; eine Falle legen — to set a trap; ein Komma legen/setzen); sich legen — to lie down; to subside, to die down
he/she/it looks for, searches; you (pl.) look for (third-person singular and second-person plural present of suchen; wer sucht, der findet — seek and you shall find); Sucht (die) — addiction, craving
run!, go! (singular imperative of laufen; lauf nicht so schnell — don't run so fast); Lauf (der) — run, race; course (im Lauf der Dinge — in the course of things); barrel (of a gun)
cash, in cash (bar bezahlen — to pay cash; in bar — in cash); Bar (die) — bar (for drinks); (literary, + genitive) devoid of, without (bar jeder Vernunft)
sweet, cute (inflected form of süß; süße Träume — sweet dreams; der süße Junge — the cute boy); Süße (die) — sweetness; sweetener; sweetie, darling (of a woman)
nearer, closer (comparative of nah; er kommt näher — he's coming closer; der Termin rückt näher); (attributive) further, more precise, more detailed (nähere Angaben — further details)
hit!, strike! (singular imperative of schlagen; schlag ein — high five, schlag nach — look it up); Schlag (der) — blow, hit; beat, stroke; type, sort
whole, entire (strong/mixed nominative/accusative neuter singular of ganz; sein ganzes Geld — all his money); Ganzes (das) — a whole
I need (colloquial first-person singular present of brauchen, for brauche; ich brauch deine Hilfe — I need your help); Brauch (der) — custom, tradition
same, alike (inflected form of gleich; die gleichen Probleme — the same problems); gleichen (verb) — to resemble, to be like

to be enough, to suffice; to pass, to hand; to reach, to extend (verb reichen; das Geld wird reichen — the money will be enough); also the inflected adjective reich — rich (einer reichen Familie — of a wealthy family; die Reichen — the rich)
brothers (nominative/accusative/genitive plural of Bruder — der Bruder; er hat drei Brüder — he has three brothers); brethren (religious or archaic use)
white (inflected form of the adjective weiß; einen weißen Hund — a white dog); Weißen — white people (inflection of Weiße); weißen (verb) — to whitewash, to whiten
closed, shut (first/third-person singular preterite of schließen; er schloss die Tür — he closed the door); Schloss (das) — castle, palace; lock, padlock
just now, right now (colloquial short form of gerade; Tom macht grad Tee — Tom is making tea right now); Grad (der) — degree (of temperature, of an angle, academic)
pains, aches (plural of Schmerz — der Schmerz; ich habe Schmerzen — I'm in pain); schmerzen (verb) — to hurt, to ache, to be painful

explains; explained (third-person singular present and past participle of erklären; das erklärt alles — that explains everything); declared, pronounced (er wurde für tot erklärt — he was declared dead); erklärt (adj.) — avowed, professed
follow! (singular imperative of folgen; folge mir — follow me); I follow (first-person singular present); Folge (die) — consequence; sequence; episode
get on!, get in!, climb! (singular imperative of steigen; steig ein — get in, steig auf das Pferd — get on the horse); Steig (der) — steep path, footpath
plans (nominative/accusative/genitive plural of Plan — der Plan; ich musste meine Pläne ändern — I had to change my plans)
bad (inflected form of schlecht; ein schlechter Anfang — a bad start); worse (comparative of schlecht; es wird schlechter — it's getting worse)
some, a few (dative plural of einige; in einigen Tagen — in a few days); sich einigen — to agree, to come to an agreement; einigen — to unite, to unify

Gang (der) — corridor, hallway; aisle (Fenster oder Gang? — window or aisle?); gear (of a car); course (of a meal); gait, way of walking; motion, progress, the way things go (etwas in Gang setzen — to set something in motion; der Gang der Welt — the way of the world)

rights (plural of Recht — das Recht; ich kenne meine Rechte — I know my rights); right (inflected form of the adjective recht; das rechte Bein — the right leg); Rechte (die) — the right hand; the political right
I keep watch; I wake up (first-person singular present of wachen / aufwachen; ich wache früh auf — I wake up early); Wache (die) — guard duty, sentry duty; guard post; vigil, wake

of this, of that — genitive singular of αυτός/αυτό, and so also 'his, its' (η αξία αυτού του σπιτιού — the value of that house; εκτός αυτού — besides that); a separate colloquial, regional adverb αυτού means 'there', but it is not what earns this rank.

give — the perfective form of δίνω (díno): 3rd person singular after θα/να and the nonfinite with έχω (να μου δώσει μια εξήγηση — for him to give me an explanation); δίδω is the learned Katharévousa variant of the same verb, not the modern lemma.

Miss, Ms — the written abbreviation Δις for δεσποινίς (Δις Τζόουνς — Miss Jones); as a word in its own right δις is the learned adverb 'twice' (formal — everyday Greek says δύο φορές), and in news writing δις abbreviates δισεκατομμύριο, 'billion'.

strengths, forces — plural of η δύναμη, power/strength (Ο Τομ έχει πολλές δυνάμεις — Tom has many strengths; με όλες μας τις δυνάμεις — with all our might); also armed forces, and in church usage the Powers, an order of angels.

secrets — plural of το μυστικό (Όλοι έχουν μυστικά — everyone has secrets; είμαι καλός στο να κρατάω μυστικά — I'm good at keeping secrets); also the neuter plural of μυστικός 'secret', and as an adverb 'secretly'.

stupid, idiotic — feminine singular of ηλίθιος, also its neuter plural (Είσαι απίστευτα ηλίθια — you're unbelievably stupid; μια αρκετά ηλίθια ερώτηση — a pretty stupid question); the same form is the adverb 'stupidly, foolishly'.

wanker, arsehole, idiot — ο μαλάκας, the everyday term of abuse for a man and one of the most common words in spoken Greek; the vocative μαλάκα cuts both ways: a real insult in anger (Γαμημένε μαλάκα! — fucking asshole!) and a friendly 'mate, dude' between friends. The literal sense 'masturbator' is rarely the point. Vulgar.

jokes — plural of το αστείο (Ο Τομ μας είπε μερικά αστεία — Tom told us some jokes; δεν σηκώνω αστεία — I can't take jokes); also the feminine singular and neuter plural of αστείος 'funny', and as an adverb 'in a funny way'.

free — accusative masculine singular and neuter singular of ελεύθερος (πολύ ελεύθερο χρόνο — a lot of free time; άφησε ελεύθερο το πουλί — let the bird loose); as a neuter noun, το ελεύθερο is freestyle swimming, or permission to do something.
sun — accusative of ο ήλιος (Λατρεύω τον ήλιο — I love the sun; έχει ήλιο και κάνει ζέστη — it's sunny and hot); the identical neuter noun το ήλιο is the chemical element helium.

uncle — accusative of ο θείος (Έμεινα με το θείο μου — I stayed with my uncle; θα επισκεφθεί τον θείο του — he will visit his uncle); the neuter το θείο is sulphur in chemistry, and 'the divine' in religious writing.

real, true — neuter plural of αληθινός (Αυτά τα διαμάντια δεν είναι αληθινά — these diamonds aren't real; τα όνειρα να γίνουν αληθινά — for dreams to come true); the same form is the adverb 'truly, really'.

sweet — neuter plural of γλυκός (Όνειρα γλυκά! — sweet dreams!); as a noun, τα γλυκά are sweets, cakes and desserts (Όλα μου τα γλυκά είναι νόστιμα — all my sweets are delicious); as an adverb, 'sweetly, gently'.
on it, on top of it (the pronominal adverb er + op — het lijkt erop dat, it seems that; hij staat erop, he insists on it; duw erop, push it); also following, next in de dag erop — the day after
weeks (plural of week — drie weken geleden, three weeks ago; de deadline is over drie weken, the deadline is three weeks from now); rarely a verb, to soak, to soften

a right, entitlement (het recht om te zwijgen — the right to remain silent; recht hebben op, to be entitled to); law, justice; also straight, upright (zit recht — sit up straight; recht vooruit, straight ahead)
bad, poor — the -e form of slecht (het slechte nieuws, the bad news; slechte vrienden; een slechte vertaling); as a noun, de slechte — the bad one, the bad guys
to ask, to pose: een vraag stellen — to ask a question; to state, to put forward (wij stellen dat, we hold that); to position, to place; also plural of stel — couples, sets

use: I use; use! (present and imperative of gebruiken — gebruik je hersenen, use your brain; ik gebruik geen drugs); as a noun, use, custom, practice (buiten gebruik — out of order; gebruik maken van, to make use of)
put, lay: I put, I lay; put!, lay! (present and imperative of leggen — leg dat boek neer, put that book down; leg het uit, explain it); also a noun, the laying of eggs

formerly, in the past, in the old days — used to (vroeger was alles beter, everything used to be better; Tom was vroeger een slaaf, Tom used to be a slave; net als vroeger, just like before); also earlier (comparative of vroeg) and former, of former times (in vroeger dagen, in days gone by)

send: I send; send! (present and imperative of sturen — stuur mij een foto, send me a photo; stuur versterking, send reinforcements); also I steer, I drive; as a noun, het stuur — steering wheel, handlebars

appetite, hunger (ik heb geen trek — I'm not hungry; trek hebben in, to fancy); also I pull; pull! (present and imperative of trekken — trek de stekker eruit, unplug it); a migration, a trek; a feature, a trait

fall: I fall; fall! (present and imperative of vallen — val dood, drop dead; val aan, attack; val me niet lastig, don't bother me); as a noun, a trap, a snare (het is een val — it's a trap), and a fall
need, have to: I need; you need in hoef je (present of hoeven, used mainly with niet — ik hoef niet met je te praten, I don't need to talk to you; je hoeft niet te komen); also a noun, hoof

walk, run: I walk; walk! (present and imperative of lopen — loop niet zo snel, don't walk so fast; loop jij naar school?); also a noun, course, duration (in de loop van de dag — in the course of the day), and the barrel of a gun
to send (het boek naar mij te sturen — to send me the book; kun je dat per e-mail sturen?); also to steer, to drive, to guide

seemed, looked (like): I/he/she/it seemed (singular past of lijken — ze leek niet blij, she did not seem happy; het leek erop dat, it seemed that; leek hij op een dokter?, did he look like a doctor?); also a noun, layman, non-expert
thought (past participle of denken): dat had ik nooit gedacht — I'd never have thought that; ik heb erover gedacht — I've thought about it; also a rare noun, opinion
to share: je werk met anderen delen — to share your work with others; also to divide, to split up (delen door — to divide by); and the plural of deel — parts
learned, studied (past participle of leren): ik heb veel van je geleerd — I learned a lot from you; jong geleerd is oud gedaan; also an adjective, erudite, scholarly, educated

advice, counsel (de raad): hij vroeg om mijn raad — he asked for my advice; also a council, board (gemeenteraad — town council); and I advise; guess! (present and imperative of raden) — raad eens, guess what
to arrange, to sort out, to see to: dat zal ik voor je regelen — I'll arrange that for you; also to regulate, to control
map (of an area): ik heb een kaart van de wereld — I have a map of the world; also a card — playing card, postcard, bank card; and a menu (of a restaurant)
dead (inflected form of the adjective dood): een dode vogel — a dead bird; ik zie dode mensen — I see dead people; as a noun, de dode — a dead person, a fatality

I stab, I stick; stab!, stick!, put! (present and imperative of steken): steek je hand op — raise your hand; steek de straat over — cross the street; also a noun, de steek — a sting, a stab, a stitch, as in iemand in de steek laten, to let someone down
costs: it costs; he/she/it costs (present of kosten) — hoeveel kost het? how much does it cost?; also a noun, de kost — board, keep, livelihood, as in de kost verdienen, to earn a living

on which, to which (relative): de manier waarop hij praat — the way he talks; een vraag waarop er geen antwoord is — a question there's no answer to; what … on/for (question) — waarop wacht je? what are you waiting for?; also whereupon, after which
I hit, I touch; hit!, touch! (present and imperative of raken): raak dit niet aan — don't touch this; also an adjective, on target, well-aimed — een rake opmerking, a telling remark

the first letter of the Dutch alphabet: wie a zegt, moet ook b zeggen — in for a penny, in for a pound; also in abbreviations such as a.u.b. (alstublieft) — please; and a rare noun, de a — a small stream, chiefly in place names like de Aa
put, placed, set (past participle of zetten): ik heb het in uw kamer gezet — I put it in your room; also an adjective, stout, stocky, and (of a term or date) fixed, set
last, most recent (superlative of laat): voor het laatst — for the last time; as an adverb, recently, the other day — laatst dacht ik aan je, the other day I thought of you
fallen (past participle of vallen): ik ben in het water gevallen — I fell into the water; in slaap gevallen — fallen asleep; also the plural of geval — cases, instances
to dream; also the plural of droom — dreams: het meisje van mijn dromen, the girl of my dreams
I hit, I strike; hit!, strike! (present and imperative of slaan): sla me niet — don't hit me; sla linksaf, sla rechtsaf — turn left, turn right; also a noun, de sla — lettuce, salad
we/they saw (past plural of zien): we zagen hem nergens — we didn't see him anywhere; also a verb, to saw, and colloquially to nag, to go on
legs (plural of het been): hij heeft lange benen — he has long legs; also bones, since been is both leg and bone; as an adjective, made of bone
drink: I drink; drink! (present and imperative of drinken): Ik drink geen koffie — I don't drink coffee; also a noun, a drink, a beverage, and in Belgium a drinks reception
books (plural of boek); also a verb, to book, to reserve, to record; vooruitgang boeken — to make progress
tracks, traces; railway tracks (plural of spoor): Steek de sporen niet over — don't cross the tracks; also a verb, to spur; to travel by train; to be consistent, to add up
turn: I turn; turn! (present and imperative of draaien); draai je om — turn around; also a noun, a turn, a bend, a rotation
buy: I buy; buy! (present and imperative of kopen); as a noun, a purchase, a deal; te koop — for sale
arranged, sorted out, taken care of (past participle of regelen); also an adjective and adverb, regular, regularly
places, spots, seats (plural of plaats); also a verb, to place, to put; to qualify (in sports)
murders (plural of moord); also a verb, to kill, to murder — the everyday transitive verb is vermoorden
shot: I/he/she shot (singular past of schieten); iets schoot me te binnen — something came to mind; also a noun, the lap (op schoot — on someone's lap)
older (comparative of oud): drie jaar ouder dan ik — three years older than me; ouder worden — to grow older; also a noun, a parent (usually plural, ouders)
wrote: I/he/she wrote (singular past of schrijven): Wie schreef dit boek? — Who wrote this book?; also a noun, a line, a stroke of the pen; a serif; over de schreef gaan — to go too far
known (past participle of weten): had ik dat geweten — had I known that; also a noun, conscience (het geweten)
leave, depart: I leave; leave! (present and imperative of vertrekken): Ik vertrek morgen — I leave tomorrow; also a noun, departure, and a room, quarters
answers (plural of antwoord); also a verb, to answer, to reply
live, reside: I live, you live (present of wonen): Ik woon hier — I live here; Waar woon je? — Where do you live?; as a noun only inside compounds (woonplaats — place of residence)
to cost; to take, require (time, effort); also the plural of kost — costs, expenses
fog, mist (de mist); also he/she/it misses, is missing (present of missen): Tom mist een tand — Tom is missing a tooth
of the (genitive of de, surviving in fixed and formal phrases): de koning der dieren — the king of the animals; de loop der tijd — the course of time; de som der delen — the sum of the parts
stories, tales (plural of verhaal); also a verb, to recount, and to recover (costs) from someone
times, occasions (plural of keer): verschillende keren — several times; meerdere keren — several times over; also a verb, to turn, to turn over, and terugkeren — to return
called, named (past participle of noemen): hij wordt Tom genoemd — he is called Tom; genoemd naar — named after; as an adjective, aforementioned, said
strange, weird, odd (inflected form of raar): een rare vraag — a strange question; rare streken — funny business; as a noun, de rare — the odd one, the weirdo
learn, teach: I learn; learn! (present and imperative of leren): Leer deze namen uit het hoofd — learn these names by heart; also a noun, leather (het leer), and doctrine, teachings (de leer)
bags, pockets, sacks (plural of zak): Maak je zakken leeg — empty your pockets; also a verb, to sink, to drop, to lower, and to fail (an exam)
to kiss (ik zou je graag kussen — I'd like to kiss you); as a noun, het kussen — pillow, cushion (ik ben geen kussen!, I'm not a pillow); also kisses, the plural of kus
searched, looked for — past participle of zoeken (ik heb overal gezocht, I've looked everywhere; het boek waar ik naar heb gezocht); as an adjective: wanted, sought-after (een gezochte crimineel)

het wezen — a being, creature (elk levend wezen bestaat uit cellen; een buitenaards wezen, an alien); in wezen — essentially, in essence (de oorlog is in wezen voorbij, the war is essentially over); to be — an older, informal infinitive of zijn (dat kan wel wezen, that may well be), and ben wezen + infinitive: went and did something (ik ben bloed wezen geven, I went to give blood); also orphans (plural of wees)

call!, shout! — imperative of roepen (roep de politie!, call the police; roep me om zes uur, call me at six); I call, I shout; as a noun, de roep — a call, a cry; a call for, a demand (de roep om verandering, the call for change); reputation, renown
de rook — smoke (waar rook is, is vuur, no smoke without fire); also I smoke (ik rook niet, present of roken) and smelled (past of ruiken — ik rook gas)
images, pictures; footage (plural of het beeld — Sami zette de beelden op het internet, Sami posted the pictures online); also statues, sculptures
balls (plural of de bal — ballen zijn rond); balls, testicles (informal); also a verb: to clench into a fist (de vuisten ballen), to play ball
lied: I/he/she lied — past singular of liegen (hij loog tegen ons, he lied to us; je loog tegen me!, you lied to me!); also a noun: lye, caustic solution
laugh: I laugh; laugh! — present and imperative of lachen (lach me niet uit, don't laugh at me; wat lach je nou?, what are you laughing at?); as a noun, de lach — a laugh, a smile

turned on, switched on; done to someone — past participle of aandoen (zij heeft het licht aangedaan, she turned the light on; wie heeft je dit aangedaan?, who did this to you?); as an adjective: moved, touched (emotionally)

to sting, prick, stab (een wesp steekt, a wasp stings); to put, stick, insert (dingen in een doos steken, to put things in a box); oversteken — to cross (de straat oversteken); as a noun, stitches, stabs (plural of de steek)
fish (plural of de vis — vissen leven in het water, fish live in the water); also a verb: to fish, to angle; to fish for information
to step, to walk (te moe om verder te stappen, too tired to walk any further); to go out on the town (we gaan stappen); also steps (plural of de stap — de eerste stappen); to march
I sell — present of verkopen (ik verkoop bloemen, I sell flowers; ik verkoop mijn auto met verlies); as a noun, de verkoop — sale, sales (de verkoop van het huis)
choose!, pick! — imperative of kiezen (kies één persoon, choose one person); I choose; also to elect (een president kiezen); as a noun, de kies — a molar (tooth)
ways, methods (plural of de manier — op verschillende manieren, in different ways); manners, good behaviour (waar zijn je manieren?)
read: I/he/she read — past singular of lezen (gisteren las ik een interessant verhaal, yesterday I read an interesting story); also I weld (present of lassen), and a noun, de las — a weld, a joint
show!, show me — imperative of tonen (toon me je papieren!, show me your papers); I show; as a noun, de toon — tone, note (op een boze toon; de toon zetten)
cards; tickets; maps (plural of de kaart — ik heb kaarten voor rij 15, I have tickets for row 15; de kaarten delen, to deal the cards); also a verb: to play cards
harder; louder; faster — comparative of hard (zet de radio harder, turn the radio up; ik zou harder leren, I'd study harder); also a noun: a mullet, the fish
buddy, mate, pal — het maatje (Tom is mijn maatje, Tom is my buddy); a size, a notch (een maatje groter, a size bigger); also maatjesharing, young salted herring

des te + comparative — all the more, the …er (hoe eerder, des te beter, the sooner the better); the old genitive of de/dat, 'of the' (de heer des huizes, the master of the house; des avonds, in the evening); also D-flat in music

decides; decided — present and past participle of beslissen (wanneer je beslist, when you decide; hij heeft beslist dat hij gaat, he has decided he's going); as an adverb: definitely, absolutely (dat is beslist waar; beslist niet)
pulled, drew: I/he/she pulled — past singular of trekken (ze trok de deur open, she pulled the door open); wegtrekken — to drain away, to fade (alle kleur trok weg uit zijn gezicht)
de kust — coast, shoreline, seaside (drie kilometer naar de kust; we gaan naar de kust); also you kiss, he/she kisses (present of kussen — ik wil dat je me kust)
I dance; dance! — present and imperative of dansen (ik dans graag, I love to dance; dans met haar!, dance with her); as a noun, de dans — a dance (de dans ontspringen, to have a narrow escape)
question (f.); also he/she/it asks (third-person singular present indicative of preguntar); ask! (second-person singular imperative): pregunta-li, ask him
he/she/it believes, thinks (third-person singular present indicative of creure): creu que sí, he thinks so; believe! (second-person singular imperative): creu-me, believe me; also (f.) cross
according to: segons ell, according to him; in accordance with; also seconds (m. plural of segon): seixanta segons, sixty seconds; second (ordinal), plural
alone, on her own (feminine of sol): visc sola, I live alone; single, one single: ni una sola paraula, not a single word; also (f.) sole (of a shoe)

taken out, removed (past participle of treure): m'ho han tret, they've taken it from me; except, apart from; unless (tret de, tret que): tret que plogui, unless it rains; also (m.) trait, feature; shot (from a gun)
murder, killing (m.); assassination; also murdered, killed (past participle of assassinar): va ser assassinat, he was murdered
happening, going on; passing (gerund of passar): què està passant?, what's happening?; also (m., f.) passer-by
he/she/it puts, places (third-person singular present indicative of posar); put! (second-person singular imperative): posa la cadira aquí, put the chair here; also (f.) pose

he/she/it goes out, leaves, comes out (third-person singular present indicative of sortir): surt a treballar a les set, he leaves for work at seven; get out!, come out! (second-person singular imperative)

he/she/it finds (third-person singular present indicative of trobar); es troba, he/she feels, is located: es troba bé, he feels well; find! (second-person singular imperative); also (f.) a find, discovery

you (plural) do, make (second-person plural present indicative of fer): què feu?, what are you doing?; do!, make! (second-person plural imperative): feu servir, use; in literary narrative also he/she/it did, made (passat simple of fer); also (m.) fief, fiefdom
clothes, clothing (f.): la roba bruta, the dirty laundry; cloth, fabric; also he/she/it steals (third-person singular present indicative of robar)
put, placed, set (past participle of posar): hem posat un nou sostre, we've put on a new roof; also (m.) air, look, demeanour

test, exam (f.); proof, evidence: no tenim cap prova, we have no proof; also he/she/it tries, tastes (third-person singular present indicative of provar); try it! (second-person singular imperative): prova-ho, try it
known, met (past participle of conèixer): he conegut la seva germana, I've met his sister; well-known, famous; also (m., f.) acquaintance
bad (feminine of mal, used before the noun): mala sort, bad luck; mala notícia, bad news; No et facis mala sang, don't torment yourself; also (f.) mailbag

sight, eyesight (f.): va perdre la vista, he lost his sight; view: punt de vista, point of view; a primera vista, at first sight; also seen (feminine of vist, past participle of veure): l'has vista?, have you seen her?

healthy, wholesome: menjar sa, healthy food; sa i estalvi, safe and sound; also his, her (unstressed possessive, before a kinship noun): sa mare, his mother; and, in Balearic, the feminine article 'the'
deal, agreement (m.): fer un tracte, to make a deal; tracte fet, it's a deal; treatment, the way someone is treated: bon tracte; dealings, contact; also tract (in anatomy or of land)
received (past participle of rebre): he rebut la teva carta, I've received your letter; also (m.) receipt
river (m.): l'aigua d'aquest riu, this river's water; also he/she/it laughs (third-person singular present indicative of riure): qui riu últim, riu millor, he who laughs last laughs best

he/she/it calls, phones; knocks (third-person singular present indicative of trucar); call!, knock! (second-person singular imperative): truca'm si necessites ajuda, call me if you need help; also (f.) swap; shooter (large marble)

he/she/it goes down, comes down; lowers, turns down (third-person singular present indicative of baixar); go down!, turn it down! (second-person singular imperative): baixa el volum, turn the volume down; low, short (feminine of baix); also (f.) drop, fall; sick leave: estar de baixa

he/she/it leaves, goes away (third-person singular present indicative of marxar); leave!, go away! (second-person singular imperative); also (f.) march; motion, running: un tren en marxa, a moving train; posar en marxa, to start up; gear (of a vehicle)
the hell, on earth (euphemistic intensifier, a softened cony): què coi vols?, what the hell do you want?; damn!, blast! (mild exclamation); also (m.) a sailcloth hammock
mind (f.): tenir en ment, to bear in mind; the spirit; also he/she/it lies, is lying (third-person singular present indicative of mentir)
fight, struggle (f.): la lluita per la llibertat, the struggle for freedom; wrestling (the sport); also he/she/it fights, struggles (third-person singular present indicative of lluitar)
he/she/it kills (third-person singular present indicative of matar); kill! (second-person singular imperative): això em mata, this is killing me; also (f.) bush, shrub
full (feminine of ple): l'ampolla està plena, the bottle is full; full, complete: plena confiança, full confidence; also (f.) in castells, the column to the right of the rengla
go! (second-person singular imperative of anar; written vés before the 2016 reform): ves a dormir, go to sleep; ves a saber, who knows; ves per on, would you believe it; also a panel or row (rare)
half (feminine of mig): mitja hora, half an hour; les tres i mitja, half past three; la mitja part, halftime; also (f.) stocking; knitting: fer mitja, to knit
running (gerund of córrer): està corrent, he's running; also (m.) current, flow: corrent elèctric, electric current; estar al corrent, to be up to date; and ordinary, everyday: una cosa corrent

he/she/it closes, shuts; locks (third-person singular present indicative of tancar); close!, shut! (second-person singular imperative): tanca la porta, close the door; also (f.) fence, enclosure; hurdle
he/she/it shows (third-person singular present indicative of mostrar); show! (second-person singular imperative): mostra'm com es fa, show me how it's done; also (f.) sample, specimen; sign, display

he/she/it was (third-person singular preterite indicative of ser and ésser — the literary passat simple: fou nomenat president, he was appointed president; everyday Catalan says va ser); also (m.) a narrow gorge, a ravine
match, game (m.): un partit de beisbol, a baseball game; also (m.) party, political party; split, divided (past participle of partir); per pale, in heraldry

he/she/it looks for, searches for (third-person singular present indicative of buscar): busca feina, he's looking for work; look for!, search! (second-person singular imperative); also (f.) hand of a clock, pointer; a thin twig or straw
last, past (feminine singular of passat): la setmana passada, last week; also (f.) a pass, a going-over; una passada, colloquially, something amazing
promise (f.): has de mantenir la teva promesa, you must keep your promise; also fiancée, betrothed woman (feminine of promès)
open, not closed: el supermercat és obert, the supermarket is open; opened (past participle of obrir): he obert la porta, I've opened the door; also open in the sense of frank, not hidden

he/she/it calls, shouts (third-person singular present indicative of cridar); call!, shout! (second-person singular imperative): crida la policia, call the police; also (f.) call, appeal, public summons
clear, bright, light-coloured (feminine singular of clar): l'elecció està clara, the choice is clear; also (f.) white of an egg

he/she/it eats (third-person singular present indicative of menjar): ell no menja carn, he doesn't eat meat; eat! (second-person singular imperative): menja menjar ràpid, eat fast food; also (f.) dish, a tasty or fancy one

he/she/it takes out, removes, gets out (third-person singular present indicative of treure): qui treu les escombraries, the one who takes out the rubbish; take out! (second-person singular imperative); also (m.) treu, a square sail

he/she/it goes up, climbs, rises; raises, puts up (third-person singular present indicative of pujar); get in!, go up! (second-person singular imperative): puja al cotxe, get in the car; also (f.) rise, increase
done, made (feminine singular of fet, past participle of fer): la feina està feta, the work is done; also (f.) deed, notable event
followed (past participle of seguir): quin carrer has seguit?, which street did you follow?; also consecutive, in a row: tres dies seguits, three days in a row; de seguit, right away
promised (past participle of prometre): t'ho he promès, I promised you; also (m.) fiancé, betrothed
giving (gerund of donar): estava donant un discurs, she was giving a speech; also (m., f.) donor, giver
closed, shut (feminine singular of tancat, past participle of tancar): la porta és tancada, the door is closed; also (f.) sit-in, occupation protest
helping (gerund of ajudar): ella m'està ajudant molt, she's helping me a lot; also (m., f.) helper, assistant
drunk, having drunk (past participle of beure): he begut massa cafè, I've drunk too much coffee; also drunk, tipsy, intoxicated
he/she/it cuts (third-person singular present indicative of tallar): aquest ganivet no talla, this knife doesn't cut; cut! (second-person singular imperative); also (f.) size, of clothing; a carving
treated, dealt with (past participle of tractar): per ser tractat com un covard, for being treated like a coward; also (m.) treaty; treatise

he/she/it burns (third-person singular present indicative of cremar): la casa es crema, the house is burning; burn! (second-person singular imperative); also (f.) cream, both the dairy kind and a skin cream; crema catalana, the custard dessert
walking, on foot (gerund of caminar): m'aniré caminant, I'll go on foot; also (m., f.) walker, wayfarer

sense, meaning (no tiene sentido - that makes no sense; en cierto sentido - in a sense); sense, faculty (sentido del humor - sense of humour; sexto sentido - sixth sense); sin sentido - senseless, meaningless; direction, way (sentido de la orientacion - sense of direction; un solo sentido - one way); also felt - past participle of sentir (no me he sentido bien, I haven't felt well)

remains, is left - from quedar (casi no queda vino, there's hardly any wine left); queda bien - it fits, it suits (esta ropa te queda bien, these clothes suit you); is located, is (por donde queda la playa? - which way is the beach?); also el toque de queda, a curfew

heard - past participle of oir (he oido hablar de ti, I have heard about you; has oido? - have you heard?); also el oido: the (inner) ear, the sense of hearing (al oido - in someone's ear; de oido - by ear)
I remember (from recordar - lo recuerdo bien, I remember it well; recuerdo haberla visto, I remember seeing her); no recuerdo - I can't remember; also el recuerdo: a memory, a keepsake or souvenir

given - past participle of dar (me has dado tanto, you have given me so much; no me habia dado cuenta, I hadn't realised); dado que - given that, since; en un momento dado - at a given moment; also el dado, a die (tira el dado - throw the dice)

I live (from vivir - vivo en el campo, I live in the country; vivo con mis padres, I live with my parents); alive, living (sigue vivo - he's still alive); vivid, bright, intense; en vivo - live (broadcast)

step, footstep; pace (dar un paso - to take a step; un paso mas - one more step); way, passage (dar paso a - to give way to); also I pass by, I spend (time) - from pasar (me paso el dia leyendo, I spend all day reading; paso a verte manana, I'll come by to see you tomorrow)

may say, that he/she say - present subjunctive of decir (no me importa lo que diga la gente, I don't care what people say); diga lo que diga - whatever he says; say it!, go ahead (formal imperative); diga? - hello? (answering the phone in Spain)
I think (from pensar - pienso que si, I think so); pienso en ti - I'm thinking of you; pienso + infinitive - I plan to, I intend to; also el pienso, animal feed

called; has called, has knocked - past participle of llamar (alguien ha llamado a la puerta, someone knocked at the door); un lugar llamado Tierra - a place called Earth; also el llamado, a call (Latin America; Spain says la llamada)
mine (feminine - la casa es mia, the house is mine; culpa mia, my fault, my bad); of mine (after the noun: una amiga mia - a friend of mine)

put, placed; put on (clothes) - past participle of poner (donde he puesto las llaves? - where have I put the keys?; lleva puesto un abrigo azul, he has a blue coat on); el puesto - a job or post (es perfecto para el puesto, he's just right for the job), a place or rank, a market stall; puesto que - since, given that

wanted; loved - past participle of querer (siempre he querido cantar, I've always wanted to sing; nunca le ha querido nadie, nobody has ever loved him); dear (querido amigo - dear friend, opening a letter); querido - darling, sweetheart
I have just - acabo de + infinitive (acabo de llegar, I have just arrived; acabo de terminar, I've just finished); I finish, I run out - from acabar
girlfriend; fiancee; bride - the female of novio (ella es mi novia, she is my girlfriend; el padre de la novia, the father of the bride)
do it!, make - familiar imperative of hacer (haz lo que quieras, do what you want; haz que se detenga, make it stop); also el haz: a beam of light, a bundle or sheaf

come back, returned - past participle of volver (has vuelto? - you've come back?); se ha vuelto loco - he has gone mad, he has become; volver a + infinitive - to do something again (he vuelto a escribirlo, I rewrote it); also el vuelto, change from a payment (Latin America)
crazy, mad (feminine - estas loca, you're crazy; una idea loca, a crazy idea; volverse loca, to go crazy); la loca - a madwoman

may happen, that it happen - present subjunctive of pasar (pase lo que pase - whatever happens, come what may); pase! - come in!, go ahead (formal imperative: pase adentro, por favor); also el pase: a pass or permit, a pass in sport

they give; you (ustedes) give - from dar (no dan nada, they give nothing; me dan miedo, they frighten me); dan a - they look out onto, they face (las ventanas dan al sur, the windows face south); donde dan esa pelicula? - where is that film showing?; also el dan, a black-belt grade

understood - past participle of entender (no he entendido nada, I haven't understood a thing; le habia entendido mal, I had misunderstood him); entendido! - understood!, got it, roger; also un entendido, an expert or connoisseur

safe - nearly always in a salvo (estas a salvo, you're safe; sano y salvo, safe and sound); except, apart from (nada es seguro salvo la muerte, nothing is certain except death); salvo que - unless, except that; also I save, I rescue - from salvar

suit; dress, gown; costume, outfit (el hombre lleva un traje negro, the man wears a black suit); also I brought - preterite of traer (traje el mio, I brought mine; no traje mi anillo, I didn't bring my ring)

left, left behind; let, allowed - past participle of dejar (me ha dejado un mensaje, he has left me a message); he dejado de fumar - I have quit smoking (dejar de + infinitive); also dejado: slovenly, careless (of a person)
salt (pasame la sal - pass me the salt; echa mas sal a la sopa - add more salt to the soup); also get out!, leave!, go out! - familiar imperative of salir (sal de mi camino, get out of my way)

parts - plural of la parte (en todas partes, everywhere; algunas partes de esta ciudad, some parts of this city); the sides, the parties (ambas partes, both sides); also you split, you leave - from partir
give him/her it - dar plus the pronoun le (dale este papel, give him this paper); dale a - hit it, press it; ¡dale! - go on!, come on! (River Plate: OK, sure)
low, short (feminine - en voz baja, in a low voice; la planta baja, the ground floor); he/she lowers, gets down - from bajar; ¡baja! - get down!; also la baja: sick leave, a drop
second (feminine - la segunda vez, the second time; de segunda mano, second-hand; la Segunda Guerra Mundial); also la segunda: second gear
aunt (mi tía tiene tres hijos, my aunt has three children); also tía: woman, girl - and as an address, hey (peninsular slang)
met - past participle of conocer (ya la había conocido, I had already met her); known, well-known, famous (es conocido en todo el país); un conocido - an acquaintance
I try, I am trying - from intentar (lo intento, I'm trying; intento dormir, I'm trying to sleep); also el intento: an attempt, a try (en un intento de, in an attempt to)
old (feminine - una casa vieja, an old house; su vieja madre, his old mother); also la vieja: old woman, and colloquially the wife or the mother (mi vieja)
he/she looks for, is looking for; you look for (formal) - from buscar (¿qué busca usted?, what are you looking for?); ¡busca! - look for it!; en busca de - in search of
el partido - a match, a game (¿viste el partido?, did you see the game?); a political party (su partido ganó, his party won); also split, broken - past participle of partir
I find, I meet - from encontrar (no encuentro mi cartera, I can't find my wallet); me encuentro - I feel (no me encuentro bien, I don't feel well); also el encuentro: a meeting, a match
to see me - the infinitive ver plus me (ven a verme mañana, come and see me tomorrow; puedo verme en el espejo, I can see myself in the mirror)
debido a - because of, owing to (no pudo venir debido al mal tiempo, he couldn't come because of the bad weather); owed, due - past participle of deber; como es debido - properly
tall, high (feminine - ella es tan alta como tú, she is as tall as you; en voz alta, out loud); also el alta: discharge from hospital, dar de alta - to sign someone up
skies, heavens - plural of el cielo (los cielos y la tierra, the heavens and the earth); ¡cielos! - good heavens!; ¿por qué cielos...? - why on earth...?
killed - past participle of matar (nunca he matado a nadie, I've never killed anyone); also un matado: a loser, a drudge (Latin American slang)

finished, ended - past participle of acabar (he acabado de leer el libro, I've finished reading the book; la guerra se había acabado, the war was over); acabar de + inf. can also mean to have just done something (me he acabado de comer, I've just eaten); also acabado: worn out, washed-up
brought - past participle of traer (¿qué te ha traído aquí?, what has brought you here?); also traído: worn, threadbare (of clothes)

I leave, I let - from dejar (dejo los libros aquí, I'm leaving the books here; dejo que use mi ordenador, I let her use my computer); dejar de + inf. - to stop doing something; also el dejo: a trace of an accent, an aftertaste
asked for, ordered - past participle of pedir (no he pedido esto, I didn't order this; me ha pedido ayuda, he asked me for help); also el pedido: an order for goods
may go out, that I/he/she leave - present subjunctive of salir (espero que salga bien, I hope it turns out well; cuando salga, when he leaves); ¡salga! - get out! (formal imperative)
legs - plural of la pierna (mis piernas son largas, my legs are long; estirar las piernas, to stretch your legs)
won - past participle of ganar (hemos ganado, we have won); earned (el dinero que se han ganado, the money they earned); also el ganado: livestock, cattle
white (feminine - una mentira blanca, a white lie; su cara se puso blanca, her face turned white); estar sin blanca - to be broke; also la blanca: a half note
taken; had, drunk - past participle of tomar (me he tomado un café, I've had a coffee); also tomado: hoarse (voice), and in Latin America drunk
he/she/it touches; plays (an instrument) - from tocar; me toca a mí - it's my turn (¿a quién le toca?, whose turn is it?); ¡toca! - touch it!, play it! (imperative)

gone out, left - past participle of salir (yo había salido, I had gone out; el tren ya había salido, the train had already left); salir bien/mal - to turn out well/badly (algo ha salido mal, something's gone wrong); recién salido de - fresh out of; also salido: sticking out, and vulgar horny
stop!, hold on! - the informal imperative of detener with te (detente ahí, stop there); also el detente, a protective amulet or badge
may he/she hear; (that) I/he/she hear - present subjunctive of oír (¡Dios te oiga!, from your lips to God's ears); listen, hear - formal imperative to usted; ¡oiga! - hey, excuse me
who? - plural of quién, for more than one person (¿quiénes son estas personas?, who are these people?); whom? (as an object: ¿a quiénes viste?)
past, last (feminine - la semana pasada, last week); also la pasada: a pass, a going-by; de pasada - in passing
he/she/it wins, earns; you win (formal) - from ganar (ella gana 30 dólares al día, she earns 30 dollars a day); also la gana: desire, will - tener ganas de, to feel like
strange, odd (feminine - una historia extraña, a strange story); also from extrañar: he/she misses (la extraña, he misses her); (no) me extraña que - it's no wonder that, I'm not surprised that
classes, lessons - plural of clase (tiene dos clases por la mañana, he has two classes in the morning); kinds, types, sorts; dar clases - to teach, to give lessons
I read - from leer (leo el inglés pero no lo hablo, I read English but I don't speak it); also Leo, the zodiac sign and constellation
he/she/it pays; you pay (formal) - from pagar (¿quién te paga?, who pays you?); paga - pay! (imperative); also la paga: pay, wages, a child's allowance
open (feminine - la puerta está abierta, the door is open); unlocked, accessible; dejar la puerta abierta - to leave the door open
younger; smaller, lesser - the comparative of joven and pequeño (mi hermano menor, my younger brother); el/la menor - the youngest; a minor, a child under age
black (feminine - una bolsa negra, a black bag); la negra - the black one; tener la negra, suerte negra - bad luck; also la negra: a quarter note (music)
so many, that many (tantos libros, so many books); tantos... como - as many... as; also los tantos: points, goals scored
pay, payment (el pago - forma de pago, method of payment); also I pay, I'll pay - from pagar (yo pago la cena, dinner's on me)
I stay, I remain; I'm keeping it, I'll take it - from quedar(se) (me quedo con esto, I'll take this one); also quedo: quiet, still (literary)
red (feminine - la casa roja, the red house); ponerse roja - to blush, to go red; also la Roja: the Spanish national side (in sport)
story, tale (el cuento - a short story, a fairy tale); a lie, a tall tale; also I count, I tell - from contar (cuento contigo, I'm counting on you)
known, found out - past participle of saber (si lo hubiera sabido, if I had known); heard (no he sabido nada de ella, I haven't heard from her); es sabido que - it is well known that
he/she/it kills; you kill (formal) - from matar (lo que no te mata te hace más fuerte, what doesn't kill you makes you stronger); also la mata: a bush, a shrub, a plant
I put, I place; I put on (clothes) - from poner (me pongo los pantalones, I put on my trousers); me pongo - I get, I become (me pongo nervioso, I get nervous)

last, previous (ano passado = last year, semana passada = last week, mes passado = last month); (as a noun, m.) the past (nao existe futuro sem o passado = there's no future without the past); passed, been through — past participle of passar (ter passado por isso = to have been through it)
question (f.) (tenho uma pergunta = I have a question; boa pergunta = good question); (he/she/you) ask, asks — from perguntar (por que pergunta? = why do you ask?)
