let, leave — imperative and he/she/you form of deixar (deixa isso aí = leave that there; me deixa sair = let me out; deixa pra lá = forget it); (as a noun, f.) cue (in theatre)

alive, living (está vivo = he's alive; ao vivo = live, of a broadcast); lively, vivid (cores vivas = bright colours); I live — first person of viver (vivo aqui desde 1990 = I've lived here since 1990)

sense, meaning (faz sentido = it makes sense; não tem sentido = it's meaningless); direction, way (sentido único = one way); sense (sight, hearing and the rest); felt — past participle of sentir (tenho sentido = I have felt)
seen — past participle of ver (eu tinha visto = I had seen; ser visto = to be seen); visto que = given that, since; (as a noun, m.) visa
call (f.) — a phone call (fazer uma chamada = to make a call); called, named — feminine of chamado (uma mulher chamada Ana = a woman called Ana); roll call, attendance (fazer a chamada)

view (f.) (a vista é tão linda = the view is so beautiful; vista para o mar = sea view); sight, eyesight (ponto de vista = point of view; à vista = in cash, on sight); seen — feminine of visto (ela foi vista = she was seen)
calls; you call — from chamar (como você se chama? = what's your name?; ele me chama = he calls me); call! (imperative); (as a noun, f.) flame
choice (f.) (não temos escolha = we have no choice; essa é a minha escolha = this is my choice); choose! — imperative and subjunctive of escolher (escolha entre estes dois = choose between these two)

takes, carries, takes (time) — from levar (quanto tempo leva? = how long does it take?; ele leva as mulheres a sério = he takes women seriously); take it! (imperative); (as a noun, f.) a batch, a wave of people
in him, in it; on him, on it — contraction of em + ele (pensei nele = I thought about him; havia algo nele = there was something in it); feminine nela, plurals neles, nelas
mind (f.) (ter em mente = to bear in mind; mente aberta = an open mind); (he/she/you) lie, lies — from mentir (ele mente = he's lying; ele nunca mente = he never lies)

test, exam (f.) (a prova é às 16h00 = the test is at 4 p.m.; como foi a prova? = how did the exam go?); proof, evidence (não há prova = there's no proof); race, sporting event; (he/she/you) taste, try on, prove — from provar
called, named — past participle of chamar (um homem chamado Tom = a man called Tom; foi chamado = he was called); (as a noun, m.) a call, a calling
control (m.) — European spelling; Brazilian Portuguese writes controle (fora de controlo = out of control); I control — first person of controlar (controlo meus pensamentos = I control my thoughts)
get out!, leave! — imperative and subjunctive of sair (saia daqui = get out of here; que ele saia = that he leave); (as a noun, f.) skirt
I speak, I talk — first person of falar (falo português = I speak Portuguese; falo sério = I'm serious; com quem eu falo? = who am I speaking to?); (as a noun, m., technical) phallus
they will be; you (plural) will be — future of ser (todos serão felizes = everyone will be happy; meninos serão meninos = boys will be boys); (as a noun, m., rare) evening work, overtime
takes off, takes out, removes — from tirar (tira as mãos = hands off; tira uma foto = take a photo); take it off! (imperative); (as a noun, f.) strip, comic strip; (slang) cop
order, request (m.) (fazer um pedido = to place an order; seu pedido está pronto = your order is ready); asked for, requested — past participle of pedir (ter pedido = to have asked for)
calls, phones; turns on — from ligar (me liga = call me; liga a TV = turn on the TV; não liga = never mind, don't take any notice); (as a noun, f.) league (sports); alloy

given — past participle of dar (isto me foi dado = this was given to me; dado que = given that; em um dado momento = at a given moment); (as a noun, m.) a piece of data (plural dados = data); a die, dice
fact (m.) — Brazilian spelling of facto (o fato é que = the fact is that; de fato = in fact); (European) suit, outfit
gone — past participle of ir (tinha ido = had gone; não deveria ter ido = I shouldn't have gone); (as a noun, m.) Ido, a constructed language reformed from Esperanto

piece, part (f.) (uma peça do carro = a car part); play (theatre) (peça de teatro); ask (for)! — imperative and subjunctive of pedir (peça para ele me ligar = ask him to call me; o que quer que me peça = whatever you ask of me)
take, carry (leve isto = take this — imperative and present subjunctive of levar); (as an adjective) light, not heavy; gentle, light (of little force)
runs; run!, hurry! (he, she, você — present of correr: ele corre rápido = he runs fast; corre! = run!, hurry!); (as a noun, m., Brazilian slang) o corre = hustle, a side job or gig

plays (an instrument); touches; rings (he, she, você — from tocar: ele toca muito bem = he plays very well; o telefone toca = the phone is ringing); toca aqui! = high five!; (as a noun, f.) den, burrow; hideout
broken, split, cracked (past participle of partir: coração partido = broken heart); departed, gone (já terei partido = I'll already have left); (as a noun, m.) party (political group)

left, left behind; dumped (past participle of deixar: eu fui deixado para trás = I was left behind; ele foi deixado pela namorada = he was dumped by his girlfriend); allowed, let; (as an adjective) abandoned, neglected; indifferent
turned on, switched on (o rádio está ligado = the radio is on — past participle of ligar); connected, linked; attached to, close to (ele é ligado a ela); (colloquial) alert, switched on, aware

low; short (feminine of baixo: eu sou mais baixa que ele = I'm shorter than him; a cadeira é baixa = the chair is low); lowers, downloads (he, she, você — from baixar: Tom baixa filmes = Tom downloads movies); (as a noun, f.) discharge, sick leave; (European) a Baixa = downtown
take, grab, catch (pega a outra cadeira! = take the other chair! — imperative and 3rd person of pegar); pega leve = take it easy; (as a noun, f.) magpie
arrested; imprisoned; stuck, trapped (feminine of preso: eu estou presa = I'm trapped; você já foi presa? = have you been arrested?); (as a noun, f.) prey; fang, tusk; female prisoner

heard (past participle of ouvir: não havia som a ser ouvido = no sound was to be heard; você terá ouvido as notícias = you'll have heard the news); (as a noun, m.) ear, the inner ear; hearing (ter ouvido para música = to have an ear for music)

paid (past participle of pagar: eu sou pago por dia = I'm paid by the day; o dinheiro não vai ser pago = the money won't be paid); I pay, I'll pay (eu te pago o almoço = I'll buy you lunch — present of pagar)
open (feminine of aberto: a porta está aberta = the door is open; não deixe a porta aberta = don't leave the door open); (as a noun, f.) a break in the rain, sunny spell; clearing, glade

saw; used to see, used to watch (I, he, she, você — imperfect of ver: eu não via muita televisão = I didn't use to watch much television; ela já não o via = she hadn't seen him in a long time); (as a noun, f.) way, road, route; segunda via = duplicate copy of a document; (as a preposition) via, by way of
a little bit, a tiny bit (m., diminutive of bocado “a bit, a mouthful”: um bocadinho mais = a little bit more); chiefly European Portuguese — Brazilian Portuguese prefers um pouquinho

kills (he, she, você — from matar: enquanto você mata o tempo, o tempo mata você = while you kill time, time kills you); mata! = kill it! (mata com fogo! = kill it with fire!); (as a noun, f.) woods, forest (a Mata Atlântica = the Atlantic Forest)
east (m., compass point: o leste = the east, a leste de = east of); (European) you read (tu, preterite of ler: já leste o livro? = have you read the book yet?)

was coming, used to come (I, he, she, você — imperfect of vir: minha filha vinha me ver = my daughter used to come see me; achei que vinha hoje = I thought you were coming today); (as a noun, f.) vineyard; grapevine
paid (feminine of pago: a conta deve ser paga hoje = the bill must be paid today); pays (he, she, você — from pagar: quanto ele paga? = how much does he pay?); (as a noun, f.) payback, comeuppance
campaign (f.), whether military, electoral or advertising; an attack, charge, offensive; also ḥamala, plural of حامل: bearers, holders

got, obtained; was able to — masculine singular perfective of पाना, and after a bare stem the “managed to, could” construction (वह मदद नहीं कर पाया — he couldn't help; मैं उसे समझा पाया — I managed to make him understand); also a noun: the leg or foot of a piece of furniture (m.)

sleep — the stem of सोना, before जाना, रहा and in the imperative (सो जाओ — go to sleep; वह सो रहा है — he is sleeping); also the correlative pronoun answering जो: that one, so, therefore (जो हुआ सो हुआ — what is done is done)
eats, eat — masculine singular habitual participle of खाना, with हूँ/है (मैं चीज़ खाता हूँ — I eat cheese); also a noun: account, ledger (m.), as in a bank account (खाता खोलो — open an account)
new — feminine singular of नया, agreeing with a feminine noun (मेरी नई गाड़ी — my new car; कुछ नई बात? — anything new?)

accept, agree, believe, obey — the stem of मानना, before लेना and जाना and in the imperative (मान लो — suppose, assume; हार मत मानो — don't give up; वह मान गया — he relented); also a noun: respect, honour; pride (m.), and in technical use a measure or value
good, well — oblique/plural masculine of भला (तुम्हारे भले के लिये — for your own good; भले लोग — good people); and in भले (ही), the concessive: even if, even though, granted that

learn — the stem of सीखना, standing before रहा, लेना and the vector verbs (वह क्या सीख रहा है? — what is he learning?; मैंने बजाना सीख लिया — I learned to play); also a noun: a lesson, a moral, a piece of advice (f.)
tooth (m.) — the anusvāra spelling of दाँत (गला हुआ दांत — the decayed tooth; दाँत साफ़ करना — to brush one's teeth); separately, a Sanskritic adjective: dental; restrained, subdued

died; dead — masculine singular perfective of मरना (उसका बेटा कैसे मरा? — how did his son die?; मैं अभी तक मरा नहीं हूँ — I'm not dead yet; मरा हुआ — dead, deceased); also in मरा जा रहा हूँ — I'm dying of (hunger, thirst)

get in, get on, ride — 타다 in the intimate style (차에 타, get in the car; 모두 타, all aboard); 타다 also covers to burn, to mix into a drink (커피에 우유를 타다), and to win a prize; separately 타 (他) is a prefix meaning other, another (타 지역, other regions)

seeing, looking, the sight of something — 보다 nominalized with -기 (보기 좋아요, it looks good; 보기 싫어, I can't stand the sight of it; 보기보다 힘들다, it's harder than it looks); also an example, or the answer choices given in a test question

to give, to offer (humble, to someone senior) — 드리다 in the -(으)ㄹ determiner form (드릴 말씀이 있어요, I have something to tell you; 도와 드릴 수 있어요, I can help you); 드리다 is the humble counterpart of 주다; also a drill, the power tool

to set, to go down; to lose; to fall (of blossom) — 지다 in the -(으)ㄹ determiner form (해가 질 거야, the sun will set; 질 수 없어, I can't lose); also 질 (質), quality or a person's nature; and -질, the suffix for a repeated action (가위질, cutting with scissors)

to drink, (something) to drink — 마시다 in the -(으)ㄹ determiner form, always standing before a noun (마실 것 좀 주세요, please give me something to drink; 뭐 마실 거야?, what are you going to drink?); rarely, a country word for popping out to visit a neighbour, and a dialect form of 마을, village

glad, pleased, happy — feminine short form of рад, said by or about a woman (Я рада вас видеть — I'm glad to see you; рада за тебя — happy for you); also the Rada, a Slavic parliamentary council (Верховная Рада)

easily (Она легко это сделала — she did it easily); it is easy to, easy for someone (Его легко найти — he's easy to find); lightly, slightly (Ты легко одет — you're lightly dressed) — short neuter of лёгкий

hard, difficult; it is hard for someone (С ним тяжело иметь дело — he's hard to deal with; мне тяжело — I'm having a hard time); heavily (тяжело дышать — to breathe heavily); seriously, gravely (тяжело болен — seriously ill) — short neuter of тяжёлый

family — семья (f.) in the accusative (защитить свою семью — to protect one's family; иметь большую семью — to have a large family); seven — семь in the instrumental (между шестью и семью — between six and seven); 7× in the multiplication table (семью семь — seven sevens)

trait, feature, characteristic (f.) (общая черта — a shared trait; семейная черта — a family trait); line, stroke; boundary, limit (черта города — the city limits; за чертой бедности — below the poverty line); distinct from чёрта, the genitive of чёрт, devil (какого чёрта — what the hell), which keeps its ё

years — год (m.) in the nominative/accusative plural (те годы — those years; спустя годы — years later; лучшие годы моей жизни — the best years of my life); years, ages, a long stretch of time (на это уходят годы — it takes years)

days — день (m.) in the nominative/accusative plural (в наши дни — these days, nowadays; в те дни — in those days; в ближайшие дни — in the next few days); one's days, one's life (его дни сочтены — his days are numbered)

female friend (f.) — the female counterpart of друг (Элис — лучшая подруга Марии — Alice is Maria's best friend; Мы подруги — we're friends); girlfriend, in the romantic sense (у тебя новая подруга — you've got a new girlfriend)

part — часть (f.) in the instrumental (быть частью чего-то — to be part of something; голова является частью тела — the head is a part of the body); mostly, for the most part (большей частью); partly, in part (as an adverb)
small, young — class 2 (wa-) form of -dogo, agreeing with plural people and animals; on its own, the little ones, the younger ones (sg. mdogo, a younger sibling)
wicked, evil — class 2 (wa-) form of -ovu, agreeing with plural people; on its own, the wicked, evildoers (sg. mwovu, a wicked person)
walls — plural of ukuta (class 11/10), as in kuta za nyumba (the walls of the house); also the verb -kuta, to come upon, find, and to satisfy
sides, directions — plural of upande (class 11/10), as in pande zote mbili (both sides); a separate noun pande is a large piece, a chunk (5/6, pl. mapande)
big, large, great — class 2 (wa-) form of -kubwa, agreeing with plural people and animals (nyoka wakubwa, big snakes); on its own, elders, seniors, bosses (sg. mkubwa)
graves, tombs — plural of kaburi (class 5/6); collectively a cemetery, graveyard (locative makaburini, at the cemetery)
yesterday (nilikuja jana, I came yesterday); in time phrases, last — usiku wa jana, last night; an unrelated jana is a larva or grub
to arrange, organise, plan, set up; also to rent (a room), and to live together; the homograph panga is machetes, plural of upanga (class 11/10)
to estimate, to reckon, to gauge (กะว่า — “I reckon…”, “I was planning to…”); a work shift, a rotation (เข้ากะ); also the casual spoken spelling of กับ (with, and) and of แก่ (to, for)
horse (classifier: ตัว); also a low bench or stool, and the knight in chess
September — the clipped everyday form of กันยายน, ordinary in speech and in on-screen dates (ปลายเดือนกันยา, 5 กันยา); also, in literary and poetic Thai, a girl or maiden
laterite, the reddish tropical rock used for building (ศิลาแลง); in Northern and Isan speech, evening (มื้อแลง); also seen as a casual spelling of แมลง (insect)

second-person singular imperative of çekmek: pull!, draw!, take! (kenara çek — pull over, fişi çek — pull the plug, para çek — withdraw money); also a cheque, a check (çek defteri — chequebook); Çek: Czech, a Czech
second-person plural imperative of gelmek: come!, come in! (polite or plural: lütfen gelin — please come, geri gelin — come back); also a bride; a daughter-in-law or sister-in-law
pain, suffering, ache; grief, sorrow (acı çekmek — to suffer, acı vermek — to hurt); as an adjective: bitter, acrid; hot, spicy (acı biber — hot pepper); painful, tragic
horse (at nalı — horseshoe); knight (in chess); also the second-person singular imperative of atmak: throw!, toss! (topu at — throw the ball, göz at — take a look, imza at — sign)

second-person singular negative imperative of bakmak: don't look!, don't look at (bana bakma — don't look at me, kusura bakma — sorry, no offence); also the verbal noun of bakmak: looking, looking after

speech, talk; conversation (konuşma yaptı — he made a speech, konuşma şekli — his way of speaking); also the second-person singular negative imperative of konuşmak: don't talk!, don't speak! (çok hızlı konuşma — don't speak so fast)

seven (saat yedi — seven o'clock, on yedi — seventeen); just as often the third-person singular past of yemek: ate, had (ekmek yedi — he ate bread, kafayı yedi — he went crazy, dayak yedi — he got a beating)
all of a sudden, suddenly (birden ünlü oldu — she suddenly became famous); also the ablative of bir: from one (birden ona kadar — from one to ten), and in birden fazla / birden çok — more than one
second-person plural imperative of almak: take!, get!, have! (polite or plural: lütfen birini alın — please take one, nefes alın — take a breath); also a forehead, brow (alın yazısı — fate, destiny)

black, dark (kara bulutlar — dark clouds, kara delik — black hole, kara tahta — blackboard); dark-skinned, brunette; grim, hard; evil (kara gün — a hard time, a rainy day; kara sevda — hopeless love, lovesickness); also as a noun: land, dry land, the mainland (kara mayını — landmine, kara hayvanı — land animal)

second-person plural imperative of kalmak: stay!, remain!, keep (polite or plural: evde kalın — stay at home, hatta kalın — hold the line); also thick, viscous; (of a voice) deep; (of a vowel) back — kalın ünlü, a back vowel
third-person singular aorist of gitmek: goes, he/she/it goes (habitually) (işe gider — goes to work, gelir ve gider — comes and goes); also an expense, expenditure; a drain
locative of dünya: in the world, on earth (dünyada kaç ülke var — how many countries are there in the world); as an emphatic with a negative: never, not for anything (dünyada olmaz — no way)
verbal noun of gitmek: going, the act of going (gitme zamanı — time to go); also the second-person singular negative imperative of gitmek: don't go!, don't leave!

work, working; study, research (çalışma saatleri — working hours, çalışma alanı — field of study, Çalışma Bakanlığı — Ministry of Labour); also the second-person singular negative imperative of çalışmak: don't work!, don't try! (çok sıkı çalışma — don't work too hard)
plural of bayan: women, ladies (bayanlar tuvaleti — the ladies' room); in address: ladies (bayanlar ve baylar — ladies and gentlemen)
third-person singular future of almak: will take, will get, will buy (zaman alacak — it will take time, satın alacak mısın — are you going to buy it); also a receivable, money owed, credit; a claim

search (arama ve kurtarma — search and rescue, arama izni — a search warrant); a (phone) call (arama yapmak — to make a call); also the second-person singular negative imperative of aramak: don't call!, don't look for! (beni arama — don't call me)
first-person singular possessive of iç: my inside, my insides, my heart (içim rahat — I'm at ease, içimden geçti — it crossed my mind); also a sip, a draught (bir içim su — a mouthful of water)

first-person singular negative past of anlamak: I didn't understand, I didn't catch that (soyadınızı anlamadım — I didn't catch your last name); on its own, as a set phrase: I don't understand, sorry?

third-person singular past of girmek: entered, went in, got in (eve girdi — he went into the house, sınava girdi — she sat the exam, depresyona girdi — he got depressed); also, in computing: an input, an entry

belly, abdomen, stomach (stem karn-: karnım ağrıyor — my stomach hurts); womb; also karı + second-person possessive: your wife (karın nasıl? — how's your wife?), and kar + genitive/possessive: of the snow, your snow
memory, recollection; memoir, reminiscence (anılarım — my memoirs); also an + accusative or third-person possessive: the moment, that moment (o anı yaşamak — to live in the moment)
second-person plural (polite) imperative of çıkmak: get out!, go out!, leave! (buradan çıkın — get out of here); rare as a noun: a small cloth bundle, a bindle

to spend or pass (time) (zaman geçirmek — to spend time); to go through, to undergo (kaza geçirmek — to have an accident); to take or carry something across, to pass something through; to see someone out; to slip on (clothing) — causative of geçmek

don't go out!, don't leave! — second-person singular negative imperative of çıkmak (dışarı çıkma — don't go outside); also the verbal noun of çıkmak: going out, leaving (çıkma teklif etmek — to ask someone out); a projecting balcony or bay window; secondhand, salvaged (part)
soru + first-person singular possessive: my question (bir sorum var — I have a question); rare as a noun in its own right: responsibility
bear (kutup ayısı — polar bear); figuratively a boor, a rude oaf; also ay + accusative or third-person possessive: the month, his month (altı ayı var — he has six months)
wife (karı koca — husband and wife); coarse slang for a woman; also kar + accusative or third-person possessive: the snow, its snow (karı severim — I love snow)
kan + accusative or third-person possessive: the blood, his/her blood (masum kanı — innocent blood; onun kanı kaynıyor — his blood is boiling); also a noun in its own right: opinion, conviction

directly, straight, right (doğrudan eve geliyorum — I'm coming straight home; doğrudan doğruya — directly, outright); as a modifier: direct (doğrudan ilişki — a direct connection) — literally the ablative of doğru
the press, the media (basın toplantısı — press conference); also basmak + second-person plural (polite) imperative: press!, push! (bir tuşa basın — press any key)

sheep (bir sürü koyun — a flock of sheep); figuratively a docile follower; also koymak + second-person plural (polite) imperative: put!, place! (şeker koyun — put in sugar); as a separate noun (koyn-): the bosom, the embrace

doktor + dative: to the doctor (doktora gittim — I went to the doctor; daha fazla doktora ihtiyaç var — there is a need for more doctors); also a noun in its own right: doctorate, PhD (doktora yapmak — to do a doctorate)
(m.) bed (au lit = to bed, in bed; se mettre au lit = to go to bed); a bed, a layer (le lit d'une rivière = a river bed); also il/elle lit = he/she reads (from lire)

(f.) sort, kind, type (une sorte de = a sort of; toutes sortes de = all kinds of); en quelque sorte = in a way; de sorte que, faire en sorte que = so that, to see to it that; also que je/il sorte = that I/he go out (subjunctive of sortir)
past participle of oublier — forgot, forgotten (j'ai oublié = I forgot; j'ai oublié ton nom = I've forgotten your name); (as adj.) forgotten, left behind

close, shut — from fermer (il ferme, je ferme; ferme la porte = close the door; ça ferme à six heures = it closes at six); ferme-la = shut up (rude); (as noun, f.) a farm; (as adj.) firm, steady (une main ferme)

(m.) market (aller au marché = to go to the market; le marché du travail); bon marché = cheap, a bargain; a deal (conclure un marché = to strike a deal); also past participle of marcher — walked, worked (j'ai marché = I walked; ça a marché = it worked)
(m.) wood, the material (une table en bois = a wooden table); a wood, the woods (dans les bois); also je/tu bois, bois ! = I/you drink, drink! (from boire)
plays, play — from jouer (il joue dehors = he's playing outside; joue avec moi = play with me); jouer à = to play (a game), jouer de = to play (an instrument); (as noun, f.) a cheek

third-person singular present of sortir — goes out, comes out (il sort ce soir = he's going out tonight; ça sort d'où ? = where does that come from?); (as noun, m.) fate, destiny; a spell (jeter un sort = to cast a spell)

past participle of recevoir — received, got (j'ai reçu ta lettre = I got your letter; bien reçu = message received); (as noun, m.) a receipt; (as adj.) accepted, widely held (une idée reçue = a conventional idea, received wisdom)
put, place — from mettre (je mets, tu mets; mets-le là = put it there; mets ton manteau = put your coat on); (as noun, m.) a dish, a prepared food (formal)

is missing, lack — from manquer (il manque un livre = a book is missing; je manque d'argent = I'm short of money); elle me manque = I miss her (the person missed is the subject); (as noun, m.) a lack, a shortage; être en manque = to be in withdrawal
feminine past participle of venir — came, come (elle est venue = she came; une idée m'est venue = an idea came to me); (as noun, f.) a coming, an arrival (la venue du printemps)

past participle of croire — thought, believed (j'ai cru = I thought, I believed; je n'en ai pas cru mes yeux = I couldn't believe my eyes); (as adj.) raw, uncooked (viande crue); (as noun, m.) a vintage, a vineyard (un grand cru)
shows, show — from montrer (montre-moi = show me; il montre du doigt = he points at); se montrer = to show up, to appear; (as noun, f.) a watch, a wristwatch
feminine of gros — big, fat, thick (une grosse voiture = a big car; une grosse voix = a deep, booming voice; une grosse erreur = a big mistake); (archaic) pregnant
past participle of tirer — pulled, drawn, shot (il a tiré trois fois = he fired three shots; tiré par les cheveux = far-fetched); être tiré d'affaire = to be out of trouble, off the hook
offers, offer — from offrir (je t'offre un verre = I'll buy you a drink; on te l'offre = it's on us); (as noun, f.) an offer, a bid; l'offre et la demande = supply and demand
touches, touch — from toucher (ne touche pas à ça = don't touch that; ça me touche = that moves me); (as noun, f.) a key, a button (on a keyboard); a touch, a stroke; en touche = out of play
changes, change — from changer (il change d'avis = he changes his mind; ne change pas = don't change); changer de = to change one thing for another; (as noun, m.) currency exchange (bureau de change)
falls, fall — from tomber (il tombe = he falls; la nuit tombe = night is falling; ça tombe bien = that's good timing); tomber amoureux = to fall in love; (as noun, f.) a grave, a tomb
feminine past participle of aller — went, gone (elle est allée = she went; elles sont allées); (as noun, f.) a path, a lane, a driveway; allées et venues = comings and goings

feminine past participle of prendre — took, taken (je l'ai prise = I took it, I took her; la place est prise = the seat is taken); (as noun, f.) a socket, a power point (prise électrique); a grip, a hold; prise de sang = blood test
past participle of ouvrir — opened (j'ai ouvert la porte = I opened the door); (as adj.) open, unlocked (c'est ouvert = it's open; à bras ouverts = with open arms); ouvert d'esprit = open-minded

(f.) an entrance, a way in (à l'entrée du bâtiment); an entry, admission (entrée libre = free admission); a starter, an appetizer (in a meal); also elle est entrée = she came in (feminine past participle of entrer)
excuse, forgive — from excuser (excuse-moi = excuse me, sorry; je m'excuse = I'm sorry); (as noun, f.) an excuse (une bonne excuse); mes excuses = my apologies
dances, dance — from danser (il danse bien = he dances well; danse avec moi = dance with me); (as noun, f.) dance, dancing (la danse classique = ballet)

puts, put down — from poser (pose-le ici = put it down here; ne pose pas tes livres sur la table = don't put your books on the table); ça ne pose aucun problème = that's no problem; poser une question = to ask a question; (as noun, f.) a pose, a posture; the laying, fitting of something

past participle of rendre — gave back, returned (je lui ai rendu son livre = I gave him back his book); made (j'ai rendu John heureux = I made John happy); rendre visite à = to pay a visit to; (as noun, m.) a render, the finished look of something

first- and second-person singular present of vivre — I live, you live (je vis ici depuis dix ans = I've lived here for ten years; c'est là que tu vis = that's where you live); also the past historic of voir: je vis = I saw (literary); (as noun, f.) a screw

short (c'est trop court = that's too short); à court de = short of (à court d'idées = out of ideas, à court d'argent = short of money); also runs — third-person singular present of courir (ce chien court très vite = that dog runs very fast); (as noun, m.) a tennis court

(m.) a permit, a licence — le permis de conduire = driving licence (as-tu le permis ? = have you got your licence?); also the past participle of permettre: allowed, permitted (est-il permis de prendre des photos ? = are we allowed to take photos here?; cela m'a permis de = that allowed me to)
cuts, cut — from couper (coupe-le en deux = cut it in half); (as noun, f.) a cut, a haircut (une coupe de cheveux); a cup, a trophy (la Coupe du monde = the World Cup); a goblet

leaves, leave — from quitter (il quitte la société = he's leaving the company; ne me quitte pas ! = don't leave me!; je te quitte demain = I'm leaving you tomorrow); (as adj.) quits, square — être quitte envers quelqu'un = to be even with someone; quitte à = even if it means

past participle of suivre — followed (je l'ai suivi dans sa chambre = I followed him into his room); took (il a suivi mon conseil = he took my advice; suivre un cours = to take a course); (as noun, m.) follow-up, monitoring, tracking
pays, pay — from payer (ce travail ne paie pas = this work doesn't pay; paie l'addition = pay the bill); tout se paie = everything has its price; also spelled paye; (as noun, f.) pay, wages

brings, bring along — from amener (je t'amène = I'll give you a lift; l'argent n'amène pas toujours le bonheur = money doesn't always bring happiness; je vous l'amène demain = I'll bring it to you tomorrow); (as adj., literary) pleasant, affable

(f. pl.) letters — plural of lettre: written letters (j'ai écrit trois lettres hier soir = I wrote three letters last night) and letters of the alphabet; les lettres = literature, the humanities (une fac de lettres = an arts faculty)

past participle of jeter — threw, thrown (qui a jeté une pierre à mon chien ? = who threw a stone at my dog?; il devrait être jeté en prison = he should be thrown in prison); jeter un coup d'œil = to take a look; (as noun, m.) a jeté (ballet leap); a table runner

hides, hide — from cacher (je me demande où il se cache = I wonder where he's hiding; ne te cache pas sous le lit = don't hide under the bed); je ne te cache rien = I'm keeping nothing from you; (as noun, f.) a hiding place, a cache; (m.) a cover, a mask

knocks, hits — from frapper (on frappe à la porte = someone's knocking at the door; frappe-moi ! = hit me!; la mort frappe tous les hommes = death comes to all men); (as noun, f.) a strike, a shot, a keystroke

third-person singular present of conduire — drives, leads (mon père conduit très bien = my father drives very well; il conduit la voiture de son père = he drives his father's car); also its past participle: driven, led (nous avons conduit tour à tour = we took turns driving); (as noun, m.) a duct, a pipe

feminine past participle of tomber — fell, fallen (une pièce est tombée de sa poche = a coin fell out of his pocket; elle est tombée amoureuse = she fell in love; Paris est tombée en 1940 = Paris fell in 1940); (as noun, f.) à la tombée de la nuit = at nightfall

throws, throw — from lancer (le garçon lance une pierre = the boy throws a stone; lance-moi la balle = throw me the ball); launches, starts (lancer un projet = to launch a project); (as noun, f.) a spear, a lance; a fire hose

past participle of couper — cut (as-tu coupé le papier ? = did you cut the paper?; il a coupé un arbre = he cut down a tree); couper à travers = to cut across, take a shortcut; (as noun, m.) a coupé (two-door car); (heraldry) party per fess
er, um — hesitation filler, also spelled euh (heu... un nez... très grand = er... a very big nose); (as noun, m., rare) a hoy, a small coastal vessel

first- and second-person singular present and the imperative of lire — read (je lis l'anglais = I read English; prends un livre et lis-le ! = take a book and read it!; lis après moi = read after me); (as noun, m.) a lily — la fleur de lis
only, sole, single; unique (feminine singular of unico): ero l'unica donna 'I was the only woman', una storia unica 'a unique story'; as a noun (f.), the only one — è l'unica 'she's the only one'
try! (tu imperative of provare); tries, is trying (third-person singular present): prova ancora 'try again'; as a noun (f.), test, trial; proof, evidence; rehearsal
new (feminine singular of nuovo): la macchina è nuova 'the car is new'; as a noun (f.), a piece of news — nessuna nuova, buona nuova 'no news is good news'
I remember (first-person singular present indicative of ricordare): ora ricordo 'now I remember'; as a noun (m.), memory, recollection; souvenir, keepsake
sure, certain; safe (feminine singular of sicuro): sono sicura 'I'm sure' (woman speaking); as a noun (f.), the safety catch of a firearm
cabbage (m.): amo il cavolo 'I love cabbage'; far more often a mild expletive standing in for cazzo — che cavolo è questo? 'what the heck is this?', cavolo! 'damn!'

rest, remainder (m.); change (money) — ecco il resto 'here's your change', del resto 'besides, after all'; also first-person singular present of restare, I stay, I'm staying — resto qui 'I'm staying here'
sent (past participle of mandare): chi ti ha mandato qui? 'who sent you here?'; as a noun (m.), mandate, term of office; warrant, writ — mandato d'arresto 'arrest warrant'
beginning, start (m.): all'inizio 'at the beginning'; also first-person singular present of iniziare, I begin, I'm starting — inizio stasera 'I'm starting tonight'
alive, live; brisk, lively; vivid, intense: è ancora vivo 'he's still alive'; also first-person singular present of vivere, I live — vivo con i miei genitori 'I live with my parents'

was (third-person singular passato remoto of essere): fu amore a prima vista 'it was love at first sight' — the literary past, C1; also invariable before a name, the late — il fu Mattia Pascal 'the late Mattia Pascal'
words (plural of parola, f.): sono senza parole 'I'm speechless'; of a song, the lyrics
arrived (past participle of arrivare): non è ancora arrivato 'he hasn't arrived yet'; as an adjective of a person, successful, one who has made it
friend (f.), female friend (feminine of amico): sei la mia migliore amica 'you're my best friend' — a romantic partner is la ragazza or la fidanzata

discovered, found out; uncovered (past participle of scoprire): hai scoperto qualcosa di nuovo? 'did you find out anything new?'; as an adjective, uncovered, bare; as a noun (m.), a bank overdraft — allo scoperto 'in the red'
I'm coming, I arrive (first-person singular present indicative of arrivare): arrivo subito 'I'll be right there'; as a noun (m.), arrival; the finish line

looks for, is looking for (third-person singular present of cercare); also the tu imperative, look for, try to — cerca di non fare tardi 'try not to be late'; as a noun (f.) only in in cerca di 'in search of'

step, pace; footstep (m.): ho fatto il primo passo 'I took the first step'; passage (of a text); also first-person singular present of passare, I pass, I come by — ti passo a prendere 'I'll come pick you up'
little girl, child (f.) (feminine of bambino): quando ero bambina 'when I was a little girl'; as an affectionate form of address, baby
true, real (feminine singular of vero): la sua storia è vera 'his story is true'; as a noun (f.), a wedding ring
I wait, I'm waiting; I expect (first-person singular present indicative of aspettare): aspetto da ore 'I've been waiting for hours'; as a noun (m.), appearance, look; aspect, side, point of view

stays, remains (third-person singular present of restare); also the tu imperative, stay — resta qui con noi 'stay here with us', non ti resta che aspettare 'all you can do is wait'; as a noun (f.), the awn of an ear of grain
started, begun (past participle of iniziare): il film è già iniziato? 'has the film already started?'; as an adjective, initiated; as a noun (m.), an initiate

I bring, I take, I carry; I wear (first-person singular present indicative of portare): ti porto a casa 'I'll take you home', porto le lenti a contatto 'I wear contact lenses'; as a noun (m.), port, harbour; port (the fortified wine)

right, correct; fair, just (feminine singular of giusto): sei sulla strada giusta 'you're on the right track', la vita non è giusta 'life isn't fair'; rare and formal as a preposition, in accordance with
law (f.): è la legge 'it's the law'; also third-person singular present of leggere, reads — lui legge prima di dormire 'he reads before bed'

I meet, I run into (first-person singular present indicative of incontrare): lo incontro spesso 'I often run into him'; as a noun (m.), meeting, encounter; match, bout — l'incontro è domani 'the meeting is tomorrow'; in andare/venire incontro a, towards, to meet
used (past participle of usare): l'ho usato una volta sola 'I've only used it once'; as an adjective, used, second-hand — un'auto usata 'a used car'; as a noun (m.), second-hand goods
exit, way out (f.): dov'è l'uscita? 'where's the exit?'; a release, an outing; also feminine past participle of uscire — è uscita 'she went out'
managed to, succeeded (past participle of riuscire): sono riuscito a entrare 'I managed to get in'; as an adjective, successful, well turned out — un dolce ben riuscito 'a cake that came out well'
course (m.) — of a river, of a university; avenue; in corso 'under way, in progress'; also past participle of correre, run — sono corso via 'I ran away', ha corso così veloce 'he ran so fast'

(he/she) stops; stop! (third-person singular present indicative and informal imperative of fermare): ferma la macchina 'stop the car'; also feminine singular of fermo, still, motionless; as a noun (f.) a term of military service, a hunting dog's pointing
balls (plural of palla, f.): hai due palle 'you have two balls'; vulgar, testicles — and figuratively guts, courage: avere le palle
lieutenant (m.) — army or police rank: il tenente Rossi; rarely, present participle of tenere, holding, and an archaic adjective meaning tenacious, resistant
last, past (feminine singular of scorso): la scorsa notte 'last night', la scorsa settimana 'last week'; as a noun (f.) a quick glance, a skim — dare una scorsa
found (feminine singular past participle of trovare): l'ho trovata 'I found her/it', dove l'hai trovata? 'where did you find it?'; as a noun (f.) a bright idea, gimmick, gag

(I) look for, I am looking for (first-person singular present indicative of cercare): cerco lavoro 'I'm looking for work'; also an archaic past participle of cercare, looked for — modern Italian uses cercato

give (present subjunctive of dare, and the formal Lei imperative): mi dia qualcosa da mangiare 'give me something to eat' (formal), hai bisogno che ti dia dei soldi 'do you need me to give you some money?'; the noun senses ('goddess', obsolete 'day') are archaic and poetic

date (f.) — a calendar date: che data è oggi? 'what's the date today?'; also given (feminine singular past participle of dare): me l'ha data 'he gave it to me', data la situazione 'given the situation'
Saint (apocopic form of santo, used before a masculine name beginning with a consonant): San Diego, San Marco, San Pietro; also the archaic Greek letter san

touches; it's (someone's) turn (third-person singular present indicative of toccare, and the informal imperative touch!): ora tocca a te 'now it's your turn'; as a noun (f.) an obsolete touchstone for testing gold and the metallic cloth woven with it
lives (plural of vita, f.): le nostre vite 'our lives', ci sono vite in gioco 'there are lives at stake'; also a separate noun (f.) screw, and vine, grapevine
series (f., invariable); set, row, range; league, division — la Serie A: una serie di errori 'a series of mistakes'; also feminine plural of serio, serious, sensible: cose serie 'serious matters'

guide (f.) — a person or a handbook; driving, steering — alla guida 'at the wheel': una guida turistica 'a tourist guide'; also (he/she) drives (third-person singular present of guidare, and the informal imperative drive!): mio padre guida molto bene 'my father drives very well'
white (feminine singular of bianco): la carta è bianca 'the paper is white', è tutta bianca 'it's all white'; as a noun (f.) a white woman, the cue ball in billiards, and the given name Bianca
checked; controlled (past participle of controllare): l'ho controllato due volte 'I checked it twice'; as an adjective, controlled, self-controlled, restrained

(I) use (first-person singular present indicative of usare): uso il computer 'I use the computer', lo uso 'I use it'; as a noun (m.) use, usage, custom — fuori uso 'out of order'; as a literary adjective, accustomed to

continuous, unbroken; continually — di continuo: un rumore continuo 'a continuous noise'; also (I) continue, I keep on (first-person singular present indicative of continuare): continuo a pensarci 'I keep thinking about it'

run, running (f.); race — ha vinto la corsa 'he won the race'; trip, ride: quanto è lunga la corsa? 'how long is the ride?'; also feminine of corso, ran (past participle of correre): la bambina è corsa in casa 'the child ran into the house'

closed, shut (feminine singular of chiuso, past participle of chiudere): tieni la porta chiusa 'keep the door closed', la strada era chiusa 'the road was closed'; as a noun (f.) a sluice or canal lock, an enclosure, the closing lines of a text

managed to, succeeded in (feminine singular past participle of riuscire): sono riuscita a prendere l'ultimo treno 'I managed to catch the last train', non sono riuscita a dormire 'I couldn't sleep'; as a noun (f.) outcome, result, success
drunk, drank (past participle of bere): ho bevuto troppo 'I drank too much', hai bevuto troppo poco 'you drank too little'; as a colloquial adjective, tipsy, drunk

held, kept (past participle of tenere): l'ho tenuto con me 'I kept it with me', era tenuto in grande riguardo 'he was held in high regard'; as an adjective, obliged, bound — essere tenuto a fare qualcosa 'to be required to do something'
pay, wages (f.): il giorno di paga 'payday'; also (he/she/it) pays (third-person singular present of pagare, and the informal imperative pay!): il crimine non paga 'crime doesn't pay'

plans, arrangements; floors, storeys of a building (plural of piano, m.): non sapevo niente di questi piani 'I knew nothing about those plans', quanti piani ha questo edificio? 'how many floors does this building have?'; also masculine plural of the adjective piano, flat, level
arms (irregular feminine plural of braccio, m.): tra le mie braccia 'in my arms', gli è morta tra le braccia 'she died in his arms'; also an old unit of length, roughly a person's outstretched arms

passed, gone by (feminine singular past participle of passare): è passata una macchina 'a car went by', l'estate è passata troppo in fretta 'the summer went by too fast'; as a noun (f.) tomato purée — passata di pomodoro — and a quick glance or once-over
to leave, to go away (first-person form of andarsene, from andare + me + ne): voglio andarmene 'I want to leave', voglio soltanto andarmene a casa 'I just want to go home'

seated, sitting (feminine singular of seduto, past participle of sedersi): la bambina seduta al piano 'the girl sitting at the piano', si è seduta di fianco a me 'she sat down next to me'; as a noun (f.) a session, meeting, sitting — seduta di allenamento 'training session'

broken (feminine singular of rotto, past participle of rompere): la radio è rotta 'the radio is broken', mi sono rotta la gamba 'I broke my leg'; as a noun (f.) a course or route of a ship or plane — fare rotta per 'to head for' — and a rout, defeat
half (feminine singular of mezzo): mezza luna 'half moon', mezza bottiglia 'half a bottle'; in telling the time, half past — sono le tre e mezza 'it's half past three'

tired (feminine singular of stanco): sono stanca 'I'm tired', ero stanca 'I was tired'; also (he/she) tires, wears out (third-person singular present of stancare); as a noun (f.) a standstill, slack water
big, large; fat (feminine singular of grosso): è quella grossa 'it's the big one', sono più grossa di te 'I'm bigger than you'; as a noun (f.) a gross, twelve dozen

chicken; chick, young of an animal (m.) — pui de somn “a nap”; also you put, you place (2nd person singular of a pune: de ce pui asta aici? “why are you putting that here?”, te rog să pui asta la loc “please put this back”)
remained, stayed; left over (past participle of a rămâne: a mai rămas doar o zi “there's only one day left”, am rămas fără bani “I ran out of money”); rămas-bun “farewell”

I like (you, him); they please, they are liked (a plăcea, normally with a dative for “to like”: îmi plac câinii “I like dogs”, nu te mai plac “I don't like you anymore”); as a noun: liking (pe plac “to one's liking”)

to follow (a urma: te voi urma “I will follow you”, a urma un curs “to take a course”); also the definite form of urmă (f.) “the trace, the track”: în urma ta “behind you”, în urma accidentului “following the accident”

(that) he/she/they come — third-person subjunctive of a veni (vreau să vină “I want him to come”, i-am cerut să vină “I asked him to come”); as a noun: guilt, fault, blame (f.) — e de vină “he is to blame”
the weapon, the gun (definite form of armă, f.: pune arma jos “put the gun down”, nu s-a tras cu arma “the gun wasn't fired”); as a verb: a arma “to arm, to cock a weapon”
the team (definite form of echipă, f.: echipa noastră “our team”, echipa are nevoie de mine “the team needs me”); as a verb: a echipa “to equip”
stayed, stood, sat (past participle of a sta: cât ai stat? “how long did you stay?”, am stat acasă “I stayed at home”); as a noun: state, country (n.) — om de stat “statesman”

met (past participle of a întâlni: l-am întâlnit de multe ori “I've met him many times”, m-am întâlnit cu ea “I met up with her”); as a noun: an encounter (n.) — the ordinary word for a meeting is întâlnire

hit, struck (past participle of a lovi: de ce m-ai lovit? “why did you hit me?”, a fost lovit de o mașină “he was hit by a car”); as a noun: the hitting, the striking (n.) — the ordinary word for a blow is lovitură

fight, battle, struggle (f.) — o luptă grea “a hard fight”, am ieșit din luptă “I got out of the fight”; also he/she fights and the imperative fight! (a lupta: Luptă! “Fight!”, Ridică-te și luptă “Get up and fight”)
the table; the meal (definite form of masă, f.: pune masa “set the table”, a lua masa “to have a meal”); as a verb: a masa “to massage”
dinner, supper — the definite form of cină, f. (am pregătit cina “I made dinner”, a lua cina “to have dinner”, cina va fi gata “dinner will be ready”); as a verb: a cina “to dine”

(that) he/she/they stay, stand, sit — third-person subjunctive of a sta (spune-i să stea “tell him to stay”, las-o să stea aici “let her stay here”); as a noun: star (f.) — Venus nu este o stea “Venus is not a star”
ran, ran away, fled (past participle of a fugi: calul meu a fugit “my horse ran away”, am fugit ca să ajung la timp “I ran to get there on time”, a fugit de acasă “he ran away from home”)
the way, the manner (definite form of mod, n.: modul în care vorbește “the way he speaks”, în modul acesta “in this way”); also: the module, the unit; the modulus

escaped, got away; got rid of — a scăpa de (past participle of a scăpa: am scăpat de pericol “we escaped the danger”, n-am idee cum a scăpat “I have no idea how he got away”); also dropped, let slip (i-a scăpat paharul “he dropped the glass”); transitively: got someone out of it, saved (m-a scăpat de o amendă “he got me out of a fine”)
he/she/it sees (third-person singular of a vedea: el vede prost “he sees badly”, nu te vede nimeni “nobody sees you”); se vede “it shows, one can see”
it is worth it; he/she/it deserves (third-person singular of a merita: merită “it's worth it”, nu merită “it's not worth it”, merită văzut “it's worth seeing”)

I seem; they seem (a părea: îți par bătrân? “do I seem old to you?”, ei par mișcați “they seem moved”, mi se par prea mari “they seem too big to me”); as an adjective: even, divisible by two (număr par); as a noun: stake, pole (m.)

(that) he/she/they die — third-person subjunctive of a muri (s-ar putea să moară “they could die”, nu vrem să mai moară oameni “we don't want more people to die”); as a noun: mill (f.) — moară de vânt “windmill”
thrown, thrown away (past participle of a arunca: am aruncat-o “I threw it away”, a aruncat o piatră “he threw a stone”, am aruncat o privire “I took a look”); as an adjective: discarded, castoff

to rely on, to count on — a se baza pe (nu te poți baza pe Tom “you can't rely on Tom”, un om pe care te poți baza “a man you can count on”); to be based on, to rest on; also the definite form of bază (f.) “the base, the basis” — baza de date “the database”

wears, carries; behaves (a purta — third-person singular and imperative: poartă ochelari “he wears glasses”, poartă-te frumos “behave nicely”); as a noun: gate; (football) goal (f.) — lângă poartă “by the gate”
I wear; I carry (first-person singular of a purta: port ochelari de soare “I'm wearing sunglasses”, ce să port diseară? “what should I wear tonight?”); also a noun: port, harbour (neuter)
plays; play! (third-person singular and imperative of a juca: Tom nu joacă “Tom doesn't play”, joacă fotbal “he plays football”); as a noun: play, playing (f.) — o joacă de copil “child's play”
played (past participle of a juca: am jucat fotbal ieri “I played soccer yesterday”, m-am jucat cu fratele meu “I played with my brother”); as a noun: playing (neuter)
to us, us — the dative clitic ne in the form it takes before another clitic (ni se pare “it seems to us”, ni se va permite “we'll be allowed”, ni le-am imaginat “we imagined them”)

(that) one likes it, that it pleases — third-person subjunctive of a plăcea (sper c-o să-ți placă “I hope you'll like it”, ar trebui să-ți placă “you should enjoy this”); as a noun: plate, sheet; record (f.)
slept (past participle of a dormi: ai dormit bine? “did you sleep well?”, n-am dormit de trei zile “I haven't slept for three days”); as a noun: sleep, sleeping (neuter)
you drink (second-person singular of a bea: bei cafea? “do you drink coffee?”, ce vrei să bei? “what would you like to drink?”); rarely a noun: bey, an Ottoman title (m.)
dies, is dying (third-person singular of a muri: e păcat când moare cineva “it's a pity when somebody dies”, moare de foame “he's starving”); rarely a noun: brine for pickling (f.)
attacked (past participle of a ataca: am fost atacat “I was attacked”, a fost atacat de un urs “he was attacked by a bear”); as an adjective: afflicted, consumptive

raised, lifted; picked up (past participle of a ridica: și-a ridicat pălăria “he raised his hat”, ne-am ridicat “we stood up”); as an adjective: raised, high, rolled up; as a noun: lifting, raising (neuter)
long live …! (Trăiască Republica! “Long live the Republic!”); it is the third-person subjunctive of a trăi “to live”: e liber să-și trăiască viața “he's free to live his life”
seemed, appeared (past participle of a părea: mi s-a părut “it seemed to me”, mi-a părut rău “I was sorry”); as an adjective: apparent, seeming (not necessarily real)

the photo, the picture (definite form of poză, f.: uită-te la poza de pe birou “look at that picture on the desk”, i-a arătat poza mea “she showed him my picture”); also a verb: a poza “to pose; to photograph”
(that it) seem, appear — third-person subjunctive of a părea (bărbații vor să pară masculini “men like to look masculine”, ca să pară mai tânăr “so as to look younger”); as a noun: pear (f.); flame

discussed, talked over (past participle of a discuta: am discutat problema “we discussed the matter”, despre ce ați discutat ieri? “what did you discuss yesterday?”); as an adjective: debated, disputed

laughed (past participle of a râde: toți au râs “everybody laughed”, Tom a râs din toată inima “Tom laughed wholeheartedly”); as a noun: laughter, laugh (neuter) — nu mă puteam opri din râs “I couldn't stop laughing”; also lynx (m.)

accepted (past participle of a accepta: mi-a acceptat ideea “he accepted my idea”, au acceptat “they accepted”); as an adjective: accepted, agreed — un punct de vedere general acceptat “a commonly accepted view”
I accept (first-person singular of a accepta: accept propunerea lui “I accept his proposal”, eu nu accept invitația “I don't accept the invitation”); rarely a noun: acceptance (neuter)

I bear it, I put up with it; I can stand (first-person singular of a suporta: nu-l suport pe omul ăla! “I can't stand that man!”, nu mai suport! “I can't take it anymore!”); also a noun: support, stand, holder (neuter)

managed, coped, did well (past participle of a se descurca: cum te-ai descurcat la test? “how did you do on the test?”, Tom s-a descurcat bine “Tom did well”); literally untangled, unravelled (a descurca)
the form, the shape (definite form of formă, f.: sub forma unui cerc “in the shape of a circle”, în formă “in shape, on form”); also the infinitive a forma “to form, to create, to make up”

run, flight, escape (f.): în fugă “in a hurry”, a lua la fugă “to take flight”, am pus unul pe fugă “I put one to flight”; also the third-person subjunctive of a fugi “to run, flee”: nu-l lăsa să fugă “don't let him run”; fugue (music)
crazy, mad — masculine plural of nebun (toți sunteți nebuni “you're all crazy”); as a noun: madmen, lunatics (un cuib de nebuni “a den of crazies”); rarely a verb: a nebuni “to go mad, to drive mad”

remembered; mentioned, brought up (past participle of a-și aminti / a aminti: mi-am amintit totul “I remembered everything”, a amintit de boala ta “he mentioned your illness”); as an adjective: aforementioned

of the one, to the one — genitive-dative masculine/neuter singular of cel (mâna celui care te hrănește “the hand of the one who feeds you”); carries the superlative: vârsta celui mai în vârstă “the age of the oldest”

I move, I move house (first-person singular of a muta / a se muta: o să mă mut în Paris “I'm going to move to Paris”, nu eram în stare să mut biroul “I couldn't move the desk by myself”); as an adjective: mute, dumb, speechless — a rămas mut “he was left speechless”, film mut “silent film”
good, fine, handsome (adj. حَسَن, f. حسنة); also the Form II verb حسَّن to improve, to make better (حسّن معرفته he improved his knowledge); and the noun حُسْن goodness, beauty — حسن الحظ good luck
to be possible for (someone), can, may — almost always impersonal: يمكن أن it is possible that, يمكنك you can (يمكنك أن تفعلها — you can do it); also to enable (someone مِن to do something)
matter, affair, business (m.; pl. أمور) — ما الأمر؟ what's the matter?; order, command (m.; pl. أوامر); also the verb أمَرَ to order, to command, to instruct
yes; yes indeed, certainly (answering a question, and answering when called — نعم؟ yes?); also نَعَم livestock, cattle (m.) and the verb نَعِمَ to live in comfort
man (m.; pl. رِجال); also رِجْل leg, foot (f.; pl. أرجُل); rarely the verb رَجِلَ to go on foot
work, job, labour (m.; pl. أعمال); deed, act, action; also the verb عَمِلَ to work, to do, to make (يعمل he works, أعمل I work)
to carry out, to do, to undertake — قام بـ + verbal noun is the ordinary way to say 'do' (قام بزيارة he paid a visit); to stand up, to rise, to get up
after (prep.) — بعد ذلك after that, بعد أن after (+ verb); afterwards, yet, still (بعد الآن any more, لم … بعد not yet); also the noun بُعْد distance, dimension (m.) and the verb بَعُدَ to be far

(particle) before a past verb: already, indeed, has just — قد رأيته I have seen him (emphatic لقد); before a present verb: may, might, sometimes — قد يكون he may be; also the verb قَدَّ to cut into strips and the noun قَدّ stature, size
to me; for me; mine — the preposition لِـ with the 1st-person suffix (قال لي he told me; لي صديق I have a friend)
person, individual (m.; pl. أشخاص) — أي شخص anyone, شخص ما someone; also the verb شخَّص to diagnose, to identify
right, entitlement (m.; pl. حقوق) — يحق لـ to have the right to; truth, what is right (الحق معك you are right); حقًّا really, truly; also the verb حَقَّ to be true, to be due
self (f.; pl. أنفُس, نفوس) — the reflexive: نفسي myself, بنفسه by himself; the same (الوقت نفسه the same time); soul, psyche; also نَفَس breath (m.)
before, prior to (prep.) — قبل أن before (+ verb), من قبل before, previously; ago (قبل سنة a year ago); also the verb قَبِلَ to accept, to agree to
to find, to come across; to get, to obtain; يوجد / لا يوجد there is / there is no (the impersonal passive — لا يوجد شيء هناك there's nothing there)

like, similar to (مِثْل + noun or pronoun — أنا مثله I am like him); such as, for example (مثلًا for example); مَثَل proverb, example (m.; pl. أمثال); also the verb مثَّل to represent, to act (a role)

grandfather (جَدّ, m.; pl. أجداد); seriousness, earnestness (جِدّ) — بجدّ hard, in earnest (عمل بجد he worked hard), على محمل الجد seriously; also جِدّ 'very' before an adjective, though ordinary 'very' comes after the adjective and is spelled جدًّا, which is its own card
to happen, to occur, to take place; (with على) to get, to obtain, to receive
to make (someone do something), to cause; to put, to place, to set; (before a non-past verb) to begin to
I know — 1st sg. of عَلِمَ (ʕalima); also أَعْلَمَ (ʔaʕlama) to inform, to notify; and the elative أَعْلَم more knowledgeable, best-informed (الله أعلم “God knows best”)
you know, do you know; she knows — imperfect of عَرَفَ (ʕarafa), 2nd sg. m. and 3rd sg. f.; also تَعَرَّفَ (taʕarrafa) to get to know, to meet, to become acquainted with (على), to recognize
oh!, ugh — exclamation of surprise, dismay or pain; rarely the verb أَوَّهَ (ʔawwaha) to moan, to sigh
to be done, to be carried out — before a verbal noun it forms the passive (تم بناؤه “it was built”, تم فصلي “I was fired”); on its own to be completed, to be finished
you are, she is; (after أن) to be — imperfect of كَانَ (kāna); also تَكَوَّنَ (takawwana) to be formed, to consist of (من)
on me; I have to, I must (على + ـي); also Ali (male given name) and عَلِيّ high, lofty, exalted (adj.)
to learn (something); also you know, do you know — 2nd sg. m. of عَلِمَ (ʕalima)
(with ما or لا) to still be, to still be doing — ما زال / لا يزال “he is still …”; on its own to go away, to disappear, to cease

condition, state, situation (m./f., pl. أحوال); حالًا right away, immediately; على أية حال / على كل حال anyway, in any case; في حال (أن) in case, in the event that; also the verb حَالَ to intervene, to prevent (دون)
to let, to allow, to leave alone — chiefly the imperative دَعْ (daʕ): دعني أرى “let me see”; also وَدَّعَ (waddaʕa) to say goodbye to, to bid farewell, to see off
to feel, to sense (بـ something); to notice, to realize; also the nouns شَعْر hair (m.) and شِعْر poetry (m.)
cause, reason, motive (m., pl. أسباب); بسبب because of, on account of; also the verb سبَّب (sabbaba) to cause, to bring about
to become, to come to be (one of kāna's sisters, with an accusative predicate); literally to enter upon the morning, to wake up
to regret, to be sorry (for, على); as a noun أَسَف regret, sorrow (m.) — للأسف, مع الأسف “unfortunately”
favor, kindness, merit (m.), as in مِن فضلك “please”; also faḍḍala, to prefer, to favor one over another; and (rare) faḍala, to remain, to be left over
to stay, to remain, to be left; to last, to endure, to continue to exist
according to, in accordance with (prep., also بحسب); فحسب / وحسب — only, merely, just; also ḥasaba, to calculate, to count, to reckon, and ḥasiba, to think, to suppose, to consider
nature, disposition, character (m., pl. طِباع); بالطبع / طبعًا — of course, naturally; also ṭabaʕa, to print, to stamp, to imprint, to type (طباعة printing, مطبعة press)
shape, form, figure (m., pl. أشكال); kind, sort; بشكل — in a … way, as in بشكل عام “generally”; also šakkala, to form, to shape, to constitute
kind, type, sort (m., pl. أنواع); species, variety; as in أي نوع من “what kind of”; also nawwaʕa, to diversify, to vary
to request, to ask politely, as in أرجوك “please” and يُرجى / الرجاء “kindly, please”; to hope for, to wish for
to her, for her; she has — the preposition لِ with the suffix ‑ها; also (rare) lahā, to divert oneself, to fool around
to go out, to leave, to exit (with مِن “out of”); to come out, to emerge; to go forth, to depart
to ask for, to request; to order (food, goods); to demand, to require; to seek, to look for; also the noun ṭalab, request, application, order (m., pl. طلبات)
inside, within (prep.); the inside, the interior (n., m.), as in في الداخل “indoors”; also the active participle of دخل, entering, incoming; and (rare) dāḵala, to befall, to come over
to present, to offer, to submit; to introduce (someone); also the noun qadam, foot (f., pl. أقدام), as in كرة القدم “football”; and qadima, to arrive, to come forward, to precede
to arrive, to reach, to get to (إلى somewhere); to connect, to join, to link up; to deliver, to convey
love, affection (m.), as in الحب; also ʔaḥabba / yuḥibb, to love, to like; and ḥabb, grains, seeds, ḥabba, a grain, a pill
pain, ache (m., pl. آلام); also أ + لم, “didn't …?”, the question hamza on the negative لم, as in ألم أقل لك؟ “Didn't I tell you?”; and ʔalima, to be in pain, to ache
face (m., pl. وجوه); side, aspect, as in وجهة نظر “point of view”; also waǧǧaha, to direct, to aim, to address (a question, a charge), to send
to move, to be in motion; to set off, to depart
I go, I am going — 1st person singular imperfect of ذهب “to go”; also (rare, form IV) ʔaḏhaba, to make disappear, to remove, to take away
OK, all right, fine (as a reply, and predicatively — ฉันโอเค, “I'm OK”); to be fine, to be in good condition; to agree, to give the OK
can, to be able to (after the verb: ทำได้ — can do it); (before the verb) did, got to (a past, completed action); to get, to obtain, to receive
excellent, great, terrific (เยี่ยม! — “Great!”); (verb) to visit, to call on (someone)
sorry; excuse me, pardon me (the everyday apology, usually with ครับ/ค่ะ); to apologise (to someone), to say sorry
ah, aah (drawn-out exclamation of realisation or hesitation, frequent in subtitled speech); (verb) to open wide, to open (the mouth): อ้าปาก
Sam (man's given name, as transliterated in dubbed film and TV); (verb) to insert among, to intersperse (as grey hairs among black)
still, yet (before the verb: ยังไม่ — not yet; ยัง alone answers “not yet”); also, too; (literary) to sustain, to keep going
that (opens a reported clause after say, think, know, be named: คิดว่า — think that); to say, to tell; to scold, to tell off
Ben (man's given name, as transliterated in dubbed film and TV); (verb) to turn aside, to swerve, to divert (เบนเข็ม — to change course)
to arrive (at), to reach, to get to; to, up to, until (จาก … ถึง …); (after ทำไม, before the verb) how come, why is it that — ทำไมคุณถึงไม่มา
about, approximately, roughly (before a number: ประมาณ 50 — about 50); (verb) to estimate, to gauge, to size up
too, as well, likewise (sentence-final: ฉันด้วยเหมือนกัน — me too); the same, alike, similar (มีปัญหาเหมือนกัน — have the same problem)
to beg, to plead, to keep asking (for); won — the Korean currency (frequent in subtitled Korean film and TV)
to be (at, in), to be located; to live, to stay, to remain; (after the verb) marks an action in progress — เขากินอยู่, “he is eating”
to clear — to empty, to free of obstruction (เคลียร์ทาง); to clear up, to sort out, to settle (a misunderstanding, a debt, a backlog)
when, at, during (before a time expression: ตอนนี้ — now, ตอนเช้า — in the morning); part, section; episode (of a series); (verb) to castrate; to graft
to invite (someone to something); (before a verb, or standing alone) please, go ahead, do — เชิญนั่ง, “please have a seat”
Ian (man's given name, as transliterated in dubbed film and TV); (verb) to be cloyed, to be sick of (rich or repetitive food)
to give, to hand over; (before a clause) to let, to have someone do, so that — ทอมให้ผมรอ, “Tom kept me waiting”; for, to (benefactive)
to reserve, to book (a room, a seat, a table); (older usage) to fasten, to bind, to secure — as in จองจำ, to put in irons
gave — past stem of دادن (انجام داد “he carried out”, نشان داد “he showed”); also (noun) justice, equity; a cry, outcry
took, seized — third-person singular past of گرفتن (قرار گرفت “was situated, was placed”, صورت گرفت “took place”); also (noun) an eclipse
about, approximately (حدود ۵۰۰ نفر “about 500 people”, حدود سال ۱۹۹۰ “around 1990”); bounds, limits — plural of حد “limit”; hence the environs, vicinity of a place
arrived, reached — third-person singular past of رسیدن (به قدرت رسید “came to power”, به پایان رسید “came to an end”); also (noun) a receipt
seen — past participle of دیدن (دیده می‌شود “is seen”, آسیب‌دیده “damaged”); also (noun, literary) the eye
written — past participle of نوشتن (نوشته شده است “has been written”); as a noun, a piece of writing, a text, a post (نوشتهٔ او “his writing, written by him”)

face, surface; side — the short form of روی (رو به “facing, toward”, روبه‌رو “opposite, face to face”, از این رو “hence, therefore”); also “go!”, the imperative of رفتن; spoken only: the object marker for را
rights — plural of حق (حقوق بشر “human rights”); also law, jurisprudence (as a field of study); and salary, pay

by, at the hands of (کشف شده بدست… “discovered by…”); by hand, into the hand — a run-together spelling of به دست, which standard written Persian separates (بدست آوردن “to obtain, to gain”, بدست آمد “was obtained”)
